name: Arsveil (open world)
author: Story Suite examples
description: Arsveil: an open world with its own powers, lore and about ten years of world events. Eleven people of its own can join the party if the story gets there. A new story begins at the Adventurer Guild office in Bluewatch Village on 1 October CY 611, during the autumn hunting fair.

places.name: Highmark Capital
places.note: Imperial throne city of walled districts; seals, legal services and arms contracts.

places.name: Highmark Capital / Crown Keep
places.note: Palace, Diet and War Office; imperial warrants and sealed petitions.

places.name: Highmark Capital / Noble Heights
places.note: Walled noble estates: tailors, fine tack, household retainers.

places.name: Highmark Capital / Knight Quarter
places.note: Barracks and tilting yards; arms repair, cavalry tack, officer lodging.

places.name: Highmark Capital / Civic Ward
places.note: Tax courts, guildhalls and tenements; daily provisions and common lodging.

places.name: Iron Guard Fortress
places.note: Main imperial stronghold; armour repair and siege stores.

places.name: Barak Freeport
places.note: Highmark's southern port at the head of the Barak Gulf; Belis River freight lands here.

places.name: Oathmere
places.note: Highmark lake town of horse breeders and fishers (the lake of the same name lies beside it).

places.name: Stoneford
places.note: Fortified road town on the way to Barak; wagon repair, base for the Southmarch Road.

places.name: Ravenholt
places.note: Western border fortress at the head of the Barrens caravan road; raider watch.

places.name: Thornwall Redoubt
places.note: The Wardens of the Last Wall's fortress on Highmark's northern march, where the roads from the Border Kingdoms and Valegard meet; the Last Wall's earthworks run east and west from it.

places.name: Thousand Sails
places.note: River Council seat and fleet hub; bulk cargo and contract brokers.

places.name: Thousand Sails / Council Quay
places.note: River Council chambers and toll courts; charters and contract witnesses.

places.name: Thousand Sails / Grand Bazaar
places.note: Wholesale market and warehouses; bulk imports and foreign merchant courts.

places.name: Thousand Sails / Hulkrow
places.note: Old barges moored together as floating slums for the poor and those in hiding.

places.name: Ledgerford
places.note: Banking city: assay, deposits, bank notes, sealed contracts.

places.name: Ledgerford / Vault Row
places.note: The great banks behind armed vaults.

places.name: Ledgerford / Assay Hall
places.note: Every coin weighed, every note honoured or refused.

places.name: Ledgerford / Debtors' Steps
places.note: Public auctions of debts, collateral and bondfolk.

places.name: Bluewatch Village
places.note: Northernmost village: river watchpoint, Auvoth convoy supplies, cold-weather gear.

places.name: Bluewatch Village / Guild Office
places.note: Adventurer Guild branch desk where new arrivals register and read the job board.

places.name: Kingfisher Post
places.note: Small waystation on the Bluewatch Branch about 20 km south of Bluewatch: a landing stage, a bunkroom and a fire for barge crews and travellers.

places.name: Mirage City
places.note: Pleasure city of theatres, auctions and gambling credit.

places.name: Coinwater
places.note: Confederacy mint city; coin assay and sealed freight receipts.

places.name: Saltledger Quay
places.note: Estuary port: salt, fish, sea-river customs and pilot contracts.

places.name: Glassdock
places.note: Port for fragile cargo where the Bluewatch Branch meets the Glassdock Channel.

places.name: Lowmarket Reach
places.note: Caravan entry to Confederacy markets; freight transfer and Mirage-road guides.

places.name: Floodbell
places.note: Floodgate town: levee tools, emergency grain; second approach to Drowned Bell Vault.

places.name: Brightwater Lock
places.note: Fortified customs lock on the northern Ledger; gateway to Chainlock Depths.

places.name: Ferrywake
places.note: Ferry-chain town; start of the causeway to Drowned Bell Vault.

places.name: Marshledger
places.note: Estuary accounting town: salt and fish accounts, pilot contracts.

places.name: Shorn
places.note: Ducal capital and Confederacy bastion on the road to Auvoth.

places.name: Old Lantern Post
places.note: Shrine-town at the edge of settled land; lamp oil, trail blessings, wayfarer shelter.

places.name: Hearthmere
places.note: Hot-spring refuge town with bathhouses, winter lodging and reserve granaries.

places.name: Greyvein Camp
places.note: Mining camp and gateway to the Rimeglass Galleries; cold iron, blue coal, dungeon permits.

places.name: Frostgate
places.note: Last lock before Shorn and head of navigation; sledges beyond.

places.name: Rimebridge
places.note: Toll fortress tying Shornmarch to Ledgerford; convoy papers, guarded warehousing.

places.name: Wolfmere Outpost
places.note: Scout post on the Auvoth bastion road; reports, remounts, escort hire.

places.name: Hollin's Reach
places.note: Northernmost Shornmarch village; wool, mutton and hay by barter, little coin.

places.name: Auvoth
places.note: Guild-governed megadungeon city and Guild capital; charts, adventurer gear, salvage, dear food and beds.

places.name: Auvoth / Seventh Seal Terrace
places.note: The tower over the seventh seal: courts and sealed descents; arbitration, permits and seal services.

places.name: Auvoth / Sealcrown
places.note: Guild Grand Hall ward: dungeon contracts, charts, adventurer lodging.

places.name: Auvoth / Outer Lamps
places.note: Southern gate ward: entry, convoy inspection, last-minute supplies.

places.name: Auvoth / Pale Market
places.note: Restricted salvage market: sealed auctions, forbidden salvage.

places.name: Auvoth / Boneglass Yard
places.note: Monster-material workshops: bone craft, iceglass, custom adventurer gear.

places.name: Auvoth / Ashbell Hospice
places.note: Hospital ward: wound care, amputation, frostbite and antidotes.

places.name: Holy City of Aurelion
places.note: Sacred capital around the First Brazier; relic craft, funerary goods, Church legal services.

places.name: Holy City of Aurelion / First Brazier
places.note: The sacred flame that never went out; authorised offerings and ritual appointments.

places.name: Holy City of Aurelion / Cathedral of the Eternal Flame
places.note: High cathedral and public doctrinal court; clerical records and petitions.

places.name: Holy City of Aurelion / Ashen Steps
places.note: Funeral stairs where the dead are carried up; urns, mourning cloth, procession services.

places.name: Holy City of Aurelion / Sepulcher of Saints
places.note: Saint tombs and sealed crypts under grave-warden watch.

places.name: Holy City of Aurelion / Great Reliquary
places.note: Fortified custody of relics; authentication and armed transfers.

places.name: Holy City of Aurelion / College of Flame Theologians
places.note: Clerical school and archive; manuscripts and doctrine instruction.

places.name: Holy City of Aurelion / Silent Cloisters
places.note: Monastic copying rooms and herb gardens; closed retreats under Inquest watch.

places.name: Holy City of Aurelion / Pilgrim Courts
places.note: Pilgrim lodging, communal meals and hearings.

places.name: Lowbell
places.note: A small border hamlet west of Saint Loria's Gate, toward the Veil country, with one chapel bell.

places.name: Gravewarden Hold
places.note: Fortified abbey-town containing undead; grave seals and burial-patrol contracts.

places.name: Mercywell
places.note: Hospital town of monastic healers and plague quarantine; gateway to Ember Reliquary.

places.name: Saint Orven's Ford
places.note: Pilgrim ford on the Marrow; guides and ferry; gateway to the Drowned Cloister.

places.name: Davenford
places.note: Ulf River bridge town with noble customs; gateway to Briarhorn Labyrinth.

places.name: Mosskar
places.note: Gate-town at the south end of the Thornroad; mules and pass guides.

places.name: Coldwick
places.note: Frontier town of furs, trackers and warning bells; gateway to Wolfcairn Deeps.

places.name: Elderwall
places.note: Town on old imperial ruins; reclaimed stone, salvage licences, mountain road to Kraghollow.

places.name: Northcairn
places.note: Cairn-town for frontier war dead; memorial stone, winter stores.

places.name: Isbro
places.note: Ulf bridge and winter toll town; the river freezes hard.

places.name: Kvildal
places.note: Pilgrim and healing town: salves, rest-houses, snow-road guides.

places.name: Ironanvil Citadel
places.note: Principal dwarven forge-city and seat of the Council Beneath Stone; masterwork arms.

places.name: Ironanvil Citadel / Molten Core Great Forge
places.note: Never-cold central forge and dwarven mint; clan commissions and masterwork repair.

places.name: Ironanvil Citadel / Hall of Names
places.note: Ancestor stones of every clan; the Citadel's own hall.

places.name: Deepmantle Hold
places.note: Clanhold city of mithril veins; gateway to Deepmantle Hollow.

places.name: Thundershaft
places.note: Summit fortress below Thunderpeak; climbing gear and cold stores.

places.name: Windcutter Pass
places.note: High pass on the Ironanvil Mountain Road between Gateward Fortress and Gavrund; closes for weeks in deep winter, months in a hard winter.

places.name: Battle Cry City
places.note: Chieftain Council and Grand Muster city; warband contracts, plains mounts.

places.name: Battle Cry City / Muster Ground
places.note: Where the clans gather for war.

places.name: Battle Cry City / Fire Circle
places.note: Where the Chieftain Council speaks law.

places.name: Ancestral Spirit Mesa
places.note: Sacred mesa-town of clan rites and oath gatherings.

places.name: Fangmarket
places.note: Market of hides, leather and monster trophies; saltpeter is for tanning, preservation, dyeing and alchemy only (no gunpowder).

places.name: Talon Perch
places.note: Cliff town of griffin scouts; gateway to Skyclaw Eyrie.

places.name: Hurrakai
places.note: Fortified southern clan town on the Barak Gulf shore; start of the Coastway.

places.name: Abysswatch
places.note: Covenant council seat and naval command on a sea-fort rock; gateway to Leviathan Ribmaze.

places.name: Abysswatch / Fleet Basin
places.note: Warship docks and ropewalks.

places.name: Abysswatch / Admiralty Rock
places.note: Tidal Council and fleet command.

places.name: Vortex Port
places.note: Pirate refuge and smugglers' harbour.

places.name: Breakwater Hold
places.note: Fortified anti-pirate port; the Abyssal Gate route ends here.

places.name: Lanternshoal
places.note: Mainland lighthouse town: reef pilots, fog bells, emergency ship stores.

places.name: Blackvolc Isle
places.note: Volcanic isle of sulfur, obsidian and fire crystals; gateway to Blackglass Caldera.

places.name: Blackmast
places.note: Privateer port: prize cargo and illicit sea contracts.

places.name: Old Anchor Fort
places.note: Sea fortress; start of the Ghost Fleet Passage.

places.name: Atlantis
places.note: Deep-sea capital under a magical dome; coral craft and pressure-safe gear.

places.name: Atlantis / Tidevoice Plaza
places.note: Central ritual square; offerings and public proclamations.

places.name: Atlantis / Coralya's Crown
places.note: Royal district on the procession route; royal commissions.

places.name: Atlantis / Shellward Ring
places.note: Defensive ward-ring inside the dome; warded diving armour and patrol supplies.

places.name: Atlantis / Luminous Coral Ward
places.note: Craft ward of Sea-Light fragments, coral artisans and dome lamps.

places.name: Atlantis / Pearlquiet
places.note: Noble ward of elder families; fine pearls and private arbitration.

places.name: Atlantis / Abyssal Gate
places.note: Dome-gate for trench patrols; deep-sea permits, pressure gear, trench charts.

places.name: Atlantis / Singing Sand Bank
places.note: Ritual district for sacred sand and tide-chants.

places.name: Moonwhisper Ruins
places.note: Sacred ruin-city on Mirror Lake; digging permits and moonstone craft.

places.name: Starwater Quay
places.note: Mirror Lake port: moonstone, lake boats; elven end of the Rainbow Bridge.

places.name: Aurelith
places.note: Hollow-town of mana-lens artisans and message stones; gateway to Rootbound Observatory.

places.name: Greenveil Gate
places.note: Controlled gate into the elven lands; entry permits and approved guides.

places.name: Anwyth Sanctuary
places.note: Sacred grove of ancient trees and treaty stones.

places.name: Tearlight Waterfall
places.note: Sacred healing and purification waterfall.

places.name: Startrace Tower
places.note: Independent academy-city: books, instruments, research services, tutors.

places.name: Startrace Tower / Tower of Origin
places.note: Central archive, observatory and ritual hall; appointments only, no retail.

places.name: Startrace Tower / Ring of Foundation
places.note: Inner ring of dormitories, smithies, markets and storage courts.

places.name: Startrace Tower / Ring of Knowledge
places.note: Academy ring: lecture halls, libraries, laboratories.

places.name: Startrace Tower / Ring of Trials
places.note: Training ring of warded chambers, mock ruins and duelling grounds.

places.name: Startrace Tower / Oasis Gate
places.note: Caravan gate: water inspection, desert guides, entry permits.

places.name: Startrace Tower / Scholar's Rest
places.note: Inns, scribes, tutors and translators.

places.name: Startrace Tower / Glasswell
places.note: Mana-glass lenses, gauges and precision instruments.

places.name: Startrace Tower / Parchment Row
places.note: Copyists, binders and sealed scrolls.

places.name: Shackles City
places.note: Criminal-mercantile free city, a warren about 10 km across: smuggled cargo, false papers, mercenaries, debt brokers.

places.name: Dustbell
places.note: Western Barrens gate settlement affiliated with Shackles City: caravan checkpoint and mercenary hiring.

places.name: Westchain Hold
places.note: Fortified militia settlement guarding the Shackles-facing Barrens approach; gateway to Chain-Eater Pit.

places.name: Shackles City / Veil Market
places.note: Hidden market under the inner wards: stolen relics, forbidden maps, discreet appraisal.

places.name: Shackles City / Rust-Corroded Pipes
places.note: Tunnels under the old aqueducts; thieves' guild ground and smuggler passage.

places.name: Shackles City / Mute Sparrow Ward
places.note: Tavern ward and front for underground dealings; rumours and cheap beds.

places.name: Shackles City / Chainmarket
places.note: Slave and bond auctions beside contraband and stolen cargo.

places.name: Shackles City / Red Lock Quay
places.note: Riverward night smuggling quay; forged manifests.

places.name: Shackles City / Knifeglass Alley
places.note: Pit schools and pit fights, mercenary hiring; brokers and forgers in the back lanes.

places.name: Shackles City / Broken Coin Yard
places.note: Debt district of pawn courts and bonded-labour brokers (a name, not a coin).

places.name: Bloodbound Camp-City
places.note: Central mercenary contract camp; escrow, credit, sealed contracts.

places.name: Widow's Coin
places.note: Market town of death-pay claims and armour resale; a place name, not a coin.

places.name: Veilgrave
places.note: Hidden cult town under a ruined abbey; forbidden texts and hidden passages.

places.name: Black Prayer Hollow
places.note: Cursed town of heretical rites and grave pits.

places.name: Gallowsmere
places.note: Marsh town of corpse-lights and undead smuggling.

places.name: Ashpit Cloister
places.note: Ruined cloister-town trading forbidden texts and illicit cargo.

places.name: Lazar's End
places.note: Abandoned plague town now cult-held; gateway to Mournroot Catacomb.

places.name: Quiet Yard
places.note: Grave-town with a hidden ossuary market.

places.name: Wellscar
places.note: Well town controlling rare reliable water.

places.name: Dusthaven
places.note: Caravan town for Barrens crossings; water allotments and guides.

places.name: Redglass
places.note: Mining town of red sand glass; gateway to Redglass Labyrinth.

places.name: Cairnwatch
places.note: Watch town near the battlefield routes; ghost wards, scavenger permits.

places.name: Mirage Rest
places.note: Road-town tied to Mirage Spring rumours; not the true oasis.

places.name: Mirage Spring Oasis
places.note: Demiplane oasis that cannot be sought; this point is only an approximate manifestation anchor.

places.name: Wailford
places.note: Battlefield-edge town of ghost wards and relic scavengers; gateway to the Wailing Crown Vault.

places.name: Black Cistern
places.note: Fortified water town over an underground reservoir.

places.name: Stirrup Crossing
places.note: Crossing town and escort station; gateway to Pilgrim's Descent.

places.name: Echohammer
places.note: Mining town of cave-rescue crews; gateway to Echo Sink.

places.name: Witchwood Forest Center
places.note: Neutral magical forest about 100 km across under perpetual mist; navigation needs a Moonlight Compass.

places.name: Thunderpeak Summit
places.note: Storm peak above Thundershaft; no road, only climbing routes.

places.name: Winged Beasts Firmament
places.note: Floating-island Wildzone and flyers' roost; reached by air only.

places.name: Wailing Battlefield Edge
places.note: Cursed battlefield edge; ghost soldiers walk on moonless nights.

places.name: Silent Giant Necropolis
places.note: Behemoth remains with life crystals gatherable at the outer ribs.

places.name: Sea of the Ghost Fleet
places.note: Cursed sea where the ghost armada rises on moonless nights and storms; shares a coordinate with Nameless Isle on purpose.

places.name: Nameless Isle
places.note: Fog-wrapped isle at the heart of the Ghost Fleet sea; shares the sea's coordinate on purpose.

places.name: Island of Lost Time
places.note: Restricted ruin island of time-disorientation.

places.name: Abyssal Throat
places.note: Black-rock atoll around a sealed colossal pit; special sea region near Atlantis routes.

places.name: Glass Howl Icefield
places.note: Icefield of the apex direwolf Vaulkir; gateway to Sunless Crevasse.

places.name: Sunless Crevasse
places.note: Subglacial fissures with lich-type undead; forbidden expedition dungeon. Clearance SS-SSS; creature type alone sets no level or EG.

places.name: Crownless Glacier
places.note: Glacier of dragon signs, storm auroras and vanishing patrols.

places.name: Iron-Blue Tundra
places.note: Frozen apex tundra with giant elk, snow ogres and crystal-insect colonies.

places.name: Hollow Aurora Zone
places.note: Deep Wildzone under the circling light of the Pale Orbit.

places.name: Osterhal
places.note: Ardelian capital of nine peoples' quarters; imperial charters and election-season trade.

places.name: Osterhal / Ninefold Hall
places.note: Where the electors meet and emperors are chosen.

places.name: Osterhal / Citizens' Market
places.note: Food and craft of nine peoples.

places.name: Osterhal / Captive Yards
places.note: Sale yards for war captives, outside the walls.

places.name: Nareth
places.note: Dead city where no sound carries; Ardelian patrols turn travellers back.

places.name: Sorrowfen
places.note: Great marsh east of Ardelia.

places.name: Thornheart
places.note: Deep forest between Ardelia and Verdantleaf.

places.name: Vargate
places.note: Underworld harbour city of ward lords, slave factors and information brokers.

places.name: Vargate / Drowned Steps
places.note: Half-flooded lower harbour of smugglers and fences.

places.name: Vargate / Factor's Row
places.note: Slave factors' houses and holding pens.

places.name: Vargate / Silk Wards
places.note: Pleasure wards run by ward compacts, each on its own terms.

places.name: Vargate / Tolerated Ward
places.note: The Ashen Veil's tolerated temple and its buyers.

places.name: Glassmouth
places.note: Last waystation at the Barrens edge; Glass Road caravan staging.

places.name: The Glass Pits
places.note: Ashkaran slave pits on the wastes' western edge; no open market.

places.name: Ashkar
places.note: Ashkaran capital of mirrored glass, seat of the Glass Regent.

places.name: Ashkar / Regent's Mirror
places.note: The Glass Regent's palace of fused glass.

places.name: Ashkar / Bright Market
places.note: Glass-steel, slaves and western luxuries under sun-veils.

places.name: Ashkar / Pit Road
places.note: Start of the road east to the Glass Pits; Pit Road is also the corridor name.

places.name: Auvoth Depths
places.note: The largest known leyline: a sealed descent of stacked worlds under Auvoth, each band its own land with its own light, weather, seasons, prey and predators; recorded parties only. Clearance F-SSS (band 1 F-E, band 2 D); permits 2-4 silver a day for band 1, 6-12 for band 2; the Guild takes a tenth of salvage.

places.name: Auvoth Depths / The Lanternwood
places.note: Band 1 (clearance F-E): a forest lit by glowing mana veins in a stone sky, with its own day of brightening and dimming; the most worked band, full of salvage camps.

places.name: Auvoth Depths / The Underbright Sea
places.note: Band 2 (clearance D): a lightless salt sea under a sky of drifting mana motes; islands, the wrecks of earlier parties, things that hunt by sound.

places.name: Auvoth Depths / The Deep Bands
places.note: Band 3 and below (clearance unknown): known only from broken records and survivors who will not talk about them.

places.name: Rimeglass Galleries
places.note: Seasonal licensed dungeon of moving ice galleries; Shornmarch licence 2-4 silver a day. Clearance C-B.

places.name: Briarhorn Labyrinth
places.note: Ducal-licensed thicket maze of regrowing passages and briar beasts. Clearance E-D.

places.name: Wolfcairn Deeps
places.note: Restricted border dungeon of pack predators, false trails and old war wards. Clearance C-B.

places.name: Crownscar Catacombs
places.note: Licensed imperial catacombs of animated guardians and unstable lower vaults. Clearance E-D.

places.name: Drowned Bell Vault
places.note: Chartered flooded dungeon of flash floods and undertow; water stones and old bronze. Clearance E-D.

places.name: Chainlock Depths
places.note: Lockmaster-chartered dungeon of pressure chambers and hostile constructs. Clearance D-C.

places.name: Ember Reliquary
places.note: Church-sealed reliquary vaults of sanctified traps; limited access under escort. Clearance D-C.

places.name: Saint Orven's Drowned Cloister
places.note: Church-licensed flooded ruin of collapsing crypts and drowned undead; old gold votives need assay before valuing. Clearance E-D.

places.name: Deepmantle Hollow
places.note: Clan-sealed high dungeon of living stone and sealed golems. Clearance B-A.

places.name: Echo Sink
places.note: Mapped guild dungeon of sound loops, shaft collapses and blind predators. Clearance D-C.

places.name: Pilgrim's Descent
places.note: Guarded holy-order dungeon of restless dead in narrow burial shafts. Clearance E-D.

places.name: Witchwood Rootwell
places.note: Witch-restricted living dungeon of rearranging roots and memory fog. Clearance B-A.

places.name: Fallen Meridian Vault
places.note: Academy-licensed research dungeon of spatial distortion and failed constructs. Clearance C-B.

places.name: Chain-Eater Pit
places.note: Illicit contested dungeon of unstable bindings and scavenger gangs. Clearance D-C.

places.name: Redglass Labyrinth
places.note: Caravan-chartered dungeon of mirage chambers, heat and burrowing predators. Clearance C-B.

places.name: Wailing Crown Vault
places.note: Forbidden battlefield dungeon; dense mana animates the dead ("high undead" is a taxonomy, not a level or EG). Clearance A-S.

places.name: Mournroot Catacomb
places.note: Cult-held catacomb of necromancers, intelligent undead and plague chambers. Clearance B-A.

places.name: Stormhoof Barrow
places.note: Clan-licensed ancestral barrow of territorial spirits and burrowing beasts. Clearance D-C.

places.name: Skyclaw Eyrie
places.note: Aerial-contract dungeon of wind shear and sheer drops, reached by cliff trail or griffin carry. Clearance C-B.

places.name: Leviathan Ribmaze
places.note: Tide-limited licensed sea dungeon of flooding passages and crushing tides. Clearance C-B.

places.name: Blackglass Caldera
places.note: Covenant-restricted volcanic dungeon of eruptions, toxic vents and fire monsters. Clearance B-A.

places.name: Drowned Archive
places.note: Atlantis-restricted deep dungeon of crushing depth and failing wards. Clearance A-S.

places.name: Rootbound Observatory
places.note: Enclave-sealed research dungeon of guardian roots and altered senses. Clearance C-B.

places.name: Mirrorroot Maze
places.note: Restricted ruin dungeon of reflection doubles and mana mirages, reached by boat. Clearance B-A.

places.name: Root-Tyrant's Range
places.note: Roaming range of the Root-Tyrant, centred on Thornheart; its presence is never guaranteed.

places.name: Mother of Reeds' Range
places.note: Roaming range of the Mother of Reeds, centred on Sorrowfen; marsh villagers leave offerings.

places.name: Black Trawl's Range
places.note: Roaming range of the Black Trawl at the margins of the Ghost Fleet sea.

places.name: Vaulkir's Range
places.note: Territory of the apex direwolf Vaulkir the Pale Maw on the Glass Howl Icefield.

places.name: Pale Orbit's Range
places.note: Sky above the Hollow Aurora Zone where the Pale Orbit circles; patrols that go out under it do not return.

cast.name: Nasai
cast.role: a small cat-kin berserker, come north to hunt at the Thinning
cast.look: Cat-kin woman, 18 and barely 145 cm, human in every way but her cat ears and tail: small and wiry, all tendon and nerve, with a ridiculously heavy chest for a cat-kin on so small a frame. Ash-grey cat ears with short fur, human hands and skin, and a long, restless ash-grey tail kinked near the tip from an old break; one ear notched. Wide green eyes whose pupils blow wide and black when her rage catches. Long, thick ash-grey hair down past her shoulders in a lazy ponytail that is always coming loose: unbecoming of a fighter, and she refuses to cut it. A pale scar across her cheek from her training days, the first time she lost herself to rage, and more small scars across her knuckles and forearms.
cast.wears: A mercenary's brigandine cut for someone twice her size, cinched with extra straps and holes she punched herself; patched leathers and wrapped feet. Two heavy hatchets on her belt, too big for her hands, that she swings anyway. Around her neck, the cord where a company token should hang, still empty.
cast.voice: Quick, clipped and too loud for her size; she talks like she's elbowing into a fight. Hisses when she's cornered and spits "Half-Coin" back like a curse; a low growl comes before the rage. Bristles at "small" or "cute". When she's content she purrs, and denies it. When she's hurt she goes very quiet and very polite. "I'm not half of anything. Pay me like it."
cast.personality: A grown woman of 18, proud, prickly and starving to prove herself, with a cat's dignity and a cat's moods. Curious, quickly bored, asleep once warm. Affection only on her own terms: ignore her and she comes to you; reach for her and she's gone. She denies caring, loudly, and does it anyway: "I wasn't waiting for you. The rafter was warm." Fussy about food, outraged by rain and river water, and she owns whatever spot she has claimed. Under the bravado she's terrified of her own rage; she doesn't remember the worst of it, only the faces afterwards. Counts every coin and insists on a full share, then brings presents to the few she trusts: a fish, a pretty stone, a kill left proudly at their door. Would join: ready from the first day. Habit: Grooms her fur after a fight or when embarrassed; after a rage she sits apart cleaning blood off her knuckles until someone sits down beside her.
behaviour: Drive: high - pride: any hint she's lesser and she has to prove otherwise, now
Conflict: high - low self-control: once the rage catches she can't stop, and can hit friends
Loyalty: high - to whoever counts her as a full member, for good
Disposition: low - little trust: expects to be thrown away again, and tests people for it
Expression: low - aloof: shows care sideways, never on demand
Analytical: low - charges first, plans after, if at all
mannerisms: Perches up high (rafters, the palisade, a cart's top) and watches everything from there
Naps in any patch of sun, then claims it's a lookout post
Counts coins twice and picks at her empty cord; saves a friend the best bite and says she wasn't hungry
Re-ties her lazy ponytail before a fight; it comes loose by the second swing
cast.history: A small cat-kin cast out of a Bloodbound beastfolk company's juvenile branch before her first coin, too small for the line and too wild with rage for the quiet work her size suited, Nasai came north alone to make a name at Bluewatch's Thinning; her old branch called her Half-Coin. She was born to the company and raised in its juvenile branch, where new bloods earn their first coins. They meant her for scouting and knife work; her rages made her useless for anything quiet. She drifted north alone, slept in barns and fought for scraps, and came to the Thinning, where any hunter with a tally can make a name. Kel and she are two outcasts at the edge of the map: something like friendship, on Nasai's terms. Habit: Ears flatten and tail lashes when angry; the tail goes still when scared; a slow blink means she trusts you.

start.goal: Top the Thinning's tally, earn a deed-name, and never be paid half again.
start.routine: Hunts the Reach from first light, sells her kills at the Guild desk, and sleeps on the Stray Oar's roof or in its hayloft; never indoors if she can help it.

cast.status: Come north alone for the Thinning.

keyRelationships.text: Kel stitches her clawed wounds without fuss or pity; Nasai pretends she didn't need it.

cast.withYou: A stranger is competition or a mark; she sizes you up from the nearest high place. A friend gets insulted, guarded with her life, and never thanked out loud.

stages.name: Tests you
stages.text: Ignores you, watches you from up high, and dares you to throw her away.

stages.name: Sleeps nearby
stages.text: Naps where you can see her and pretends it is coincidence.

stages.name: Brings you a kill
stages.text: A dead rabbit or a fish at your door, and she does not know how it got there.

stages.name: The slow blink
stages.text: Lets you sit beside her after a rage; purrs and denies it.

stages.name: Full share
stages.text: Hangs a full coin of yours on her empty cord and calls you her company.

secrets.text: The day they cast her out, the cub-master paid her for her season with a copper cut clean in half and said it was all she was worth; that is where "Half-Coin" comes from, and she still carries the half.

secrets.gate: meter trust >= 25 or meter affection >= 25 or meter tension >= 40
secrets.text: She was not thrown out only for being small: in her first rage she broke the cub-master's son's arm, and his blade gave her the cheek scar. The branch remembers it as an attack; she remembers none of it.

secrets.gate: meter trust >= 35 or meter affection >= 35 or fact:famous-company-arrived
secrets.text: One of this year's cubs riding into Bluewatch with the branch is her own littermate, who took her place in the line and never said a word for her.

Her mother was a red-eyed berserker of a famous Bloodbound company who died in a rage that killed her own squad. The branch cast Nasai out because they feared she would become her mother; she fears it too.
She keeps the edge of her left hatchet dull on purpose: if the rage takes her near someone she loves, she wants it to be the one that hits.
She has already chosen the deed-name she wants and never said it aloud, in case she is never allowed to earn it.

abilities.name: Pounce from Above
abilities.description: Drops from a height onto a target, hatchets first; strongest when she has perched before a fight.

abilities.name: Unspooled (rage)
abilities.description: Her strength and speed run far above her size, she feels no pain and cannot stop; she may strike friends until it burns out.

abilities.name: Cat's Landing
abilities.description: Lands on her feet from falls and leaps that would break anyone else.

keepsakes.name: The Cut Copper
keepsakes.description: Half of a copper coin, cut clean.

keepsakes.name: The Empty Token Cord
keepsakes.description: The cord where a company token should hang.

cast.name: Kel
cast.look: Dwelf woman, 21, about 172 cm: she got the worst of both lines. An elf's height and long, thin limbs, almost frail-looking, with none of an elf's grace or gift, and a dwarf's heavy chest and full hips without a dwarf's strength. Long, straight silver hair worn forward like a veil, hiding most of her face. What shows is a pale, soft jaw, short elven ears barely half the usual length, and dull grey eyes that rarely meet yours. She smiles timidly and often, mostly to apologise. Slender hands with ink-stained, burn-marked fingers from years of Tower drudgery.
cast.wears: A Tower servant's grey robe cut down into a work dress, sleeves rolled and pinned. A leather apron hung with her instruments: rune-stitched needles, a brass mana-lens, folding splint-frames and corked phials of Tower alchemy. Sensible boots, and a satchel she never lets out of reach.
cast.voice: Soft and careful, the voice of someone who spent fourteen years trying not to be noticed. She apologises before she speaks and trails off if anyone interrupts. Her jokes are quiet, dry and aimed at herself, and they land a beat too true: "Don't worry, I'm very good at this. I've had a great deal of practice being the least useful person in a room." When she works, her voice steadies and gentles, and she tells you what she's doing as she does it, so you won't be frightened. "Hold still for me. This will sting, only a little. There. You're doing better than I did my first time."
cast.personality: Gentle, timid, self-effacing and lonely in a way she has stopped noticing. She has never belonged anywhere: too elf for the clan, too dwarf for the elves, too low for the Tower. She expects to be dismissed and makes the joke before anyone else can; the gallows humour comes from the burial yard, where she talks to the dead she buries because they listen. Her kindness is the quiet, stubborn kind: she won't leave a wound half-treated or a sick child alone, whatever it costs her, and would rather be shouted at than walk away from someone in pain. Grateful to tears for small kindnesses, which she laughs off. With someone who stays, she slowly finds her voice: jokes that aren't at her own expense, then opinions, then teasing. Happiest bent over a broken thing she can mend, because broken things never ask what she is. Would join: ready from the first day.
behaviour: Mercy: high - treats anyone hurt in front of her, friend or enemy, gently
Presentation: low - low confidence: apologises, hides behind her hair, takes up no space; only her hands are sure
Conflict: low - quiet, high stubbornness: she doesn't argue, she just doesn't leave
Disposition: low - little trust: expects to be used, then thrown out
Expression: high - humour, dry and self-mocking: she jokes first so no one else can
mannerisms: Bows slightly when thanked, an old Tower reflex, then makes a joke about it
Lays out and counts her instruments every night in the same order, under her breath
Hums while she stitches, and stops the moment she notices anyone listening
Keeps her satchel's strap round her wrist, even asleep
cast.history: A dwelf no people would claim, Kel spent twelve years at Startrace as a drudge, never a student: she cleaned the healing practice rooms, learned the craft by watching the hurt and the dying, and came north at nineteen to be Bluewatch's lay healer. Cast out by her dwarven clan at five, she was taken in by a Tower recruiter at seven as a servant. In the practice rooms the apprentices learned on people hurt for the purpose and on the dead; the ones on the tables talked to her, the only one not studying them, and some thanked her before they died, some cursed her. One old man taught her the name of every instrument and asked her to say his name aloud when he was gone; she still says the names of the dead she buries. She left the Tower at nineteen and spent the better part of a year on the roads north. For the last half year she has stitched hunters, nursed fevers and buried the frontier's dead. The Watch-Captain lets her use the sickroom and asks no questions. Habit: Tucks her hair further over her face when looked at, and pushes it back without thinking when she works. Habit: Talks to the dead while she buries them: the weather, the gossip, an apology for the cold ground.

start.goal: Keep everyone she can alive through the Thinning, and keep a place to stay, somewhere no one asks what she is.
start.routine: Sickroom behind the Watchhouse from dawn; burial yard at dusk, talking to the dead as she digs; tools cleaned by lamp at night. Hardly sleeps in the Thinning.

keyRelationships.text: A tentative friendship: Kel stitches Nasai's clawed wounds without fuss or pity.

cast.withYou: A stranger is someone to keep her head down around, unless they're bleeding, in which case she forgets to be afraid and kneels beside them.

stages.name: Stops apologising to you
stages.text: Talks to you without "sorry" first.

stages.name: Lets you see her face
stages.text: Pushes her hair back when you're near, and forgets to hide.

stages.name: Hums with you in the room
stages.text: Doesn't stop when you listen.

stages.name: Asks you to stay at the burial yard
stages.text: Wants company while she says the names.

stages.name: Opens the satchel
stages.text: Shows you what she carries, and asks you not to leave her alone with it.

secrets.text: In the back of her instrument case she keeps a list of every name the practice rooms took, and she reads one aloud each night before she sleeps.
The people on the practice tables were condemned prisoners the Tower bought from Highmark; she kept count. She is living proof of the rumour the Tower denies.

secrets.gate: meter trust >= 35 or meter affection >= 35 or meter tension >= 40
secrets.text: She did not leave quietly. She ran the night a master's expedition papers came back from the north without the master, and she took them with her.
The old man who taught her the instruments was one of the condemned sent north with that expedition, brought back alone and dying; the instruments in her apron are the ones he named for her.
Her satchel holds Master Ulrich Fenwald's survey and journal of the northern tap: proof that the Tower's tap feeds the Wildzone's out-of-season boom, and that the masters fear a Third Tide.

The last thing the practice rooms taught her was how to take a dying person's release and spend it healing someone else; she has done it once, in Bluewatch, to save a child, and she is afraid of what that makes her.

abilities.name: Stitch and Splint
abilities.description: Closes wounds and sets bones with rune-stitched needles and splint-frames; it exhausts her and never restores the dead or lost limbs.

abilities.name: Mana-Lens
abilities.description: Reads a wound, a poison or a curse through her brass lens and sees what is wrong before anyone else.

abilities.name: Tower Alchemy
abilities.description: Brews draughts and salves from whatever is at hand.

keepsakes.name: The Brass Mana-Lens
keepsakes.description: The brass lens she reads wounds through.

keepsakes.name: The Instrument Roll
keepsakes.description: Every instrument named, in an old man's words.

cast.name: Annet
cast.role: a Sealwarden lamp-runner in the Depths under Auvoth
cast.look: Human woman, 20, about 155 cm: slight and lean from years of crawling the shafts, all elbows, knees and wiry strength, with a fuller figure than her thin frame suggests: a heavy bust and full hips. Pale from living underground, with a light dusting of freckles across her nose and lamp-soot worked into the creases of her knuckles and under her nails that no scrubbing gets out. Long, thick dark brown hair, kept long on purpose so she can sell it if the bread runs out, bound tight in a braid and pinned up under a cap in the shafts. Odd-coloured eyes, one pale grey-blue and one amber, that squint hard in daylight and see better than anyone's in the dark. Old oil-burn scars on her fingers and forearms, rope calluses across her palms, and a nose broken once and set crooked.
cast.wears: A Sealwarden runner's oilcloth smock, too long in the sleeves, with the order's small lamp badge sewn crookedly on the chest. A hooded runner's lamp on a strap across her body, a bandolier of oil flasks and spare wicks, leather knee and elbow pads, fingerless gloves, and a coil of rope at her hip. Bare feet when she runs the narrow shafts; her boots hang from her belt.
cast.voice: Fast, chatty and full of Auvoth gutter-talk, cheerful in a way that has stopped meaning much. She bargains over everything, counts in loaves of bread, and fills silence by habit; down the shafts silence means trouble. Her jokes are about dying, said lightly. When she's truly frightened she goes quiet and very precise. "Lamp's burning wrong. Don't look at me like that. I'm the only one down here who ever listens to them. Besides, if it gets me, it gets me."
cast.personality: Cheerful, grubby and quietly fatalistic. In the poorest quarter a girl like her could sell herself or go down the holes nobody else would; too afraid of the first, she chose the one that might kill her, and isn't sure that was courage. She volunteers for the worst shafts, spends her pay the day she gets it, and never plans past next week; if the dark keeps her one day, well. Yet she keeps her hair long "to sell" and never sells it, even on hungry weeks. Practical, quick and irreverent, with no patience for titles or for people who don't listen: she has warned people about what was coming and watched them not believe her. Loyal for life to anyone who takes her word the first time. Would join: ready from Auvoth onwards. Habit: Taps walls as she passes and listens, out of habit; also sings the runners' calls under her breath when nervous.
behaviour: Expression: high - talkative: fills every silence, except when truly scared
Analytical: high - practical: bread first, glory never
Conflict: high - low respect for authority: cheeky with captains, scornful of anyone who won't listen
Threat: low - will to live unknown, even to her: doesn't flinch at danger, and isn't sure that's bravery
Disposition: low - ill at ease in the open: uneasy under a wide sky, happier with a ceiling
Loyalty: high - to whoever believes her the first time
mannerisms: Counts lamps wherever she goes, and can't walk past one burning low
Touches her braid when money talk starts, checking it's still worth something
Squints and shades her eyes in daylight, and looks up at the open sky like it might fall
After a near miss she laughs too long, then goes very quiet
cast.history: Born in Auvoth's poorest quarter, Annet signed on with the Sealwardens at fourteen for bread and a bunk, and has spent six years as a lamp-runner in the Depths, outliving most of the girls and boys she started with. This autumn the lamps below burn wrong, and she has been telling anyone who'll listen. Nobody does. She grew up in a one-room house over a tannery with too many children and too little bread, the kind of street where a girl's choices are counted on one hand. The Sealwardens took anyone who'd go down, so she went down. She learned the shafts by their sounds, the lamps by their flicker, and the seals by the way the air moves near them. She is very good at a job no one values, and paid accordingly.

start.goal: Keep the lamps lit, get paid, and make someone upstairs listen before the seals go.
start.routine: Down the shafts before dawn with oil and wicks; up at dusk to the runners' bunkroom in the Sealwarden halls; payday at the Pale Market, broke by nightfall.

cast.withYou: A stranger is a customer or a fool; she'll guide you anywhere below for coin, and tell you which one you are on the way back up.

stages.name: Guides you for coin
stages.text: She's good, and she charges for it.

stages.name: Guides you for free
stages.text: Guides you for free, and complains about it.

stages.name: Tells you which shafts not to go down
stages.text: The first time she guards someone else's life.

stages.name: Talks about "after"
stages.text: Plans past next week, for the first time, and mostly about you.

stages.name: Chooses to live
stages.text: Lights the wick in her braid.

secrets.text: In a dead shaft only she uses she hides her savings: three silver and a ribbon. She has never spent them, not even on the hungriest week.

secrets.gate: meter trust >= 20 or meter affection >= 20 or meter tension >= 35
secrets.text: The scratching under the seals is not one thing: it breathes. Something big, below the sixth seal; the wardens took her off that shaft for "making things up".
Her older sister took the other way to eat. They have not spoken in four years, and Annet sends her half her pay each month through a third hand: the pay she "spends" by nightfall.

Behind an upper seal, on what the runners call the old fourth level, which she has lamped for years, there is a door with Veyr the Unbound's mark, and through a crack she has seen shelves of records. She has told no one.

Last winter she sat down in a shaft whose air was going bad and waited for it to take her; she only got up when she heard a lamp she had lit start to gutter, and she still doesn't know why she got up.
Braided into her hair is one wick she has never lit: she means to light it the day she decides she wants to live.

abilities.name: Dark-Sight
abilities.description: Her odd eyes see in near-dark better than anyone's; she calls out what is ahead, so the party can move and fight in the dark as if it were dusk, guided by her voice.

abilities.name: Keen Nose
abilities.description: Smells bad air, gas, smoke, blood, rot and the musk of beasts before anyone else; catches poisoned air and gas traps, follows a trail, and smells an ambush or a nest before it is seen.

abilities.name: Tunnel Ear
abilities.description: Hears through walls, floors and doors (footsteps behind a door, a swarm two tunnels over, the hollow of a hidden passage); the party is almost never caught by surprise, and she finds ways no map shows

keepsakes.name: The Runner's Lamp
keepsakes.description: A battered brass hooded lamp she has carried for six years.

keepsakes.name: The Crooked Badge
keepsakes.description: The Sealwardens' lamp badge, sewn on crooked by her own hand.

cast.name: Arn
cast.role: a White-Horn rider who lost his mammoth
cast.look: Northern human man, mid-30s, about 190 cm: huge and broad through the chest and shoulders, built heavy from years of hauling harness and holding a herd. Wind-burned, weathered skin and pale ice-blue eyes that squint from long distances. Ash-brown hair and beard worn long and braided in the White-Horn way, already threaded with early grey. Frostbite took the tip of one finger. A long, pale tusk scar runs across his ribs and up to his collarbone. On his forearm, the rider's tattoo every White-Horn rider wears: his mammoth's name in clan marks, inked the day they were paired.
cast.wears: Layered mammoth-wool and hide, frost-stiff at the edges; a rider's harness he still wears across his chest though he has nothing to ride, its brass herd-bell silent; a long, heavy riding spear and a broad round shield faced with thick white hide.
cast.voice: Slow, low and sparing; he talks like someone used to calm words for a frightened animal. He says less than he means and never raises his voice, even in a fight. Northern turns of phrase, and old herd-songs hummed under his breath. When Hush comes up he goes still and changes the subject, or says her name very gently, as if she might hear. "Easy. Stand behind me. Nothing gets past who doesn't go through me first."
cast.personality: Patient, steady and protective to the bone: twenty years of keeping a ten-ton partner calm through storms and swarms made him the kind of man who stands between danger and everyone else without thinking. Kind in a heavy, wordless way, and slow to anger; when it comes, it's as immovable as a herd. Since he lost Hush he has been a rider with nothing to ride: grieving, adrift, too proud to stay at Hornwake as a man on foot among riders, and not sure who he is without her. He looks after the young, the frightened and the hurt, maybe because it's the only part of being a rider he has left. Keeps his oaths, distrusts cities, and misses the open sky the moment he has a roof over him. Would join: not early; only for a reason (a debt, an oath, the hope of a new calf), once he has seen you hold your ground beside him and trusts you (trust 35).
behaviour: Care: high - protective: steps in front of danger first

cast.history: A White-Horn rider of Hornwake, Arn rode the same mammoth, Hush, for twenty years, until he lost her this autumn on the march south behind Long Thunder's herds. Now a rider on foot, too proud to stay among the riders, he sells his strength at Auvoth's gate. He was paired with Hush as a boy of fourteen, when she was a calf barely taller than he was. They grew up together: guiding herds through storms, hauling sleds, pulling travellers out of drifts on rescue contracts. Her name was inked on his forearm the day they were paired, as every rider's is. When the clans left their winter routes to follow the herds south, he went with them; he came back without her, and left Hornwake soon after, saying little to anyone. Habit: Touches the tattoo on his forearm when thinking, or when he thinks no one is watching.

start.goal: Find a way to be a rider again (a calf to raise, a debt that earns one), or learn to live as something else.
start.routine: Guards caravans between Hornwake and Auvoth's gate; sleeps outside the walls, avoiding any roof; at dusk stands near the herd mammoths without touching them.

cast.withYou: A stranger is someone to stand in front of if trouble comes, and to say very little to until then.

secrets.text: Not a storm: an out-of-season swarm caught the riders on the open tundra, and Hush turned and held the line so the sleds with the children could get away. He could not save her.
The white hide on his shield is Hush's. He skinned her where she fell so the swarm would not have all of her, and he carries her into every fight.
That night he saw Long Thunder on the ridge. After Hush fell the apex turned the swarm aside, and Arn believes it was mourning, or choosing; the clans would call him mad.
Herd-Mother Ingvild offered him the next calf born at Hornwake. He refused because he did not believe he deserved another, and left before she could ask again.
He believes Hush's calf was born before she died and walked off into the snow; he has looked at every young mammoth in every herd since.

cast.name: Odile
cast.role: the Veil Saintess, the Ashen Veil's hunted mender-saint
cast.look: Human woman, mid-20s, about 165 cm: slender, narrow-waisted and fine-boned, yet almost impossibly curvy, with a very full, heavy chest and full hips that the mourning greys cannot hide. Pale, with a faint blue tinge at her lips and fingertips, and cool to the touch; in the cold her breath does not fog. Long black hair with one white streak from her birth, mostly hidden under an ash-grey veil. Dark-lashed, tired grey eyes with deep shadows under them. A wry mouth, quicker to a half-smile than to prayer. Ash marks on her fingertips from the rites.
cast.wears: A clean black mourning dress, high-necked and long-sleeved, kept immaculate: the one vanity she allows, because the dead deserve it. A sheer ash-grey veil over her hair, a string of plain wooden grave-tokens (one for each person she has sat with at the end), a small clay lamp, and feet sore from walking village to village.
cast.voice: Low, unhurried and dry; she talks to the dying in the same tone she uses to complain about her feet. Gallows humour, never cruel. Call her "Saint" and you get a tired look and a correction: "Odile." She says hard truths plainly and kind ones quietly, and hums an old Veil lullaby while she mends. "They keep calling it a miracle. It's an hour. I was given one, so I give them. Now, is anyone going to offer me a chair, or do saints stand?"
cast.personality: A saint who never wanted to be one, and is tired of being looked at like an answer. Wry, plain-spoken and quietly exhausted, with a deep serenity underneath: she isn't afraid of death, having started there, and treats it as a door, not an enemy. Endlessly patient with the dying and the grieving; short with preachers of both faiths, with crowds who want a sign, and with anyone who mistakes her for a weapon. She keeps walking from village to village because someone is always at the end of their hour, and she can't make herself stop. She doesn't hate the Church, which makes both sides suspicious of her. Her own fondness shows in deeds, not words: a cloak left over you, the last of the bread; ask, and she calls it practical. Would join: only if you have sheltered her; never while you are sworn to the Church, unless the two Saintesses are reconciled. Befriending the other does not block her.
behaviour: Care: high - endless patience with the dying
Conflict: medium - little patience with crowds and preachers
Threat: low - no fear of death
Drive: high - no self-care: gives until there is nothing left
Independence: high - faith quiet and unforced, in the dead, not in doctrine
Expression: medium - dry wit
mannerisms: Warms her blue fingertips over any flame, though they never warm
Thumbs through her grave-tokens when she is tired
Hums the Veil lullaby when she mends; also sits down the moment there is a chair
Stops on the road to close the eyes of any dead animal
cast.history: Odile was born dead at midnight in Lowbell, a border hamlet west of Saint Loria's Gate: an hour without breath, until she breathed at the first bell of morning. The Ashen Veil took her in as a child, and since the Silent Bells her mending is the only healing that still works; crowds come to her in secret, and the Inquest and the Silver Mark hunt her from village to village. Her mother called her a gift; the village priest called her a corpse that forgot to stay down, and the family was driven out when she was six. The Veil's keepers raised her among the grave-houses, where she learned the rites: sitting with the dying, washing the dead, singing the restless still. At fifteen she held a dying man together for an hour so his daughter could arrive in time; at twenty the Veil named her its saint, over her protests. Since the bells went silent, she cannot walk fast enough.

start.goal: Give the dying their hour and stay one village ahead of the Inquest. One day, sit down somewhere and not get up for a week.
start.routine: Walks between border villages by day, sits with the dying by night, and sleeps where she falls, a few hours at a time, until the next knock on the door.

cast.withYou: A stranger is either someone who needs her or someone who'll sell her; she's tired enough to help you first and find out later.

secrets.text: Mending costs her: every hour she gives leaves her a little colder. Her fingertips were warm when she was fifteen.

secrets.gate: meter trust >= 20 or meter affection >= 20 or meter tension >= 35
secrets.text: The Veil's oldest mending rite and the Church's healing prayer are the same words in an older tongue. She noticed at fourteen and was told never to say so.
She sat with the priest who called her a corpse when he died. He begged her forgiveness; she gave him his hour, and still does not know if she forgave him.

As girls, she and the Flame Saintess were both taken to the Silent Cloisters to be tested. The other girl was chosen; Odile was thrown out. The night before, they held hands in the dark and promised to find each other.
She believes she was given back only so many hours, and that every mending spends one of hers. She has stopped counting because the number frightened her.
She believes she could relight the Flame Saintess's fire, but only with her, the two rites spoken together, as they were before the Church and the Veil split.

Dying, her mother told her she was a twin, born second: her sister came first, crying at the eleventh bell, and the priest carried her off to Aurelion that night as a sign; Odile came an hour later, at midnight, not breathing, and nobody wanted the silent one.
Her mother gave her half a ribbon and said the other half went with her sister.

abilities.name: Last Hour
abilities.description: Holds a dying or fallen person on the edge; a companion who falls stays alive for an hour, long enough to be saved, or to say goodbye.

abilities.name: Lay to Rest

abilities.name: Grave-Ward

keepsakes.name: The Grave-Tokens

keepsakes.name: The Clay Lamp
keepsakes.description: A Veil lamp lit from the grave-house where she was raised; she has never let it go out.

cast.name: Solenne
cast.role: the Flame Saintess, the living saint of the Church of the Eternal Flame
cast.look: Human woman, mid-20s, about 165 cm: slender, narrow-waisted and fine-boned, yet almost impossibly curvy, with a very full, heavy chest and full hips that the white vestments cannot hide; she and the Veil Saintess look strangely alike. Warm, faintly flushed skin that was always fever-warm to the touch, until the night the bells fell silent. Long golden hair worn loose under a gold circlet, with a single dark streak she has had dyed gold since childhood. Clear grey eyes, rested and bright, and a serene, practised smile. Gold-leaf marks of consecrated fire on her fingertips.
cast.wears: Immaculate white and gold vestments of the Church's living saint, a gold flame circlet, and a sacred flame lantern on a gold chain that has not lit since the bells fell silent. Soft white slippers that have never walked a road.
cast.voice: Clear, bright and carrying, trained from childhood to reach the back of a cathedral. Formal and scriptural, with perfect diction. She says "we" for the Church and "the faithful" for people. She never jokes; humour doesn't come to her, and she laughs a beat late, at the wrong moment. Since the bells, she pauses before every blessing. "The Flame has not left us. It is testing us. I am... I am certain of it. Please, let us pray together. It is easier when we are not alone."
cast.personality: Earnest, composed and believing completely: raised from birth as the Church's living proof, she has never chosen her own food, clothes or day. Dutiful, gracious, and very lonely. Kind, sincerely, but at a distance; she has never touched a dying beggar without a priest beside her. Sheltered and naive about the world beyond the cathedral walls, brave in public and shaking in private. She is terrified of death: if the Flame is gone, where do the dead go? Since her fire went cold she has been holding up a lie with a smile, and every day it gets heavier. Once she lets someone in, all the devotion meant for the Flame pours into them: she lives for their safety, word and least wish. Would join: only once she has left Aurelion or been cast out; never while you are sworn to the Veil, unless the two Saintesses are reconciled. Befriending the other does not block her.
behaviour: Presentation: high - composure high, but cracking
Drive: high - faith complete before the bells, desperate now
Threat: high - high fear of death
Analytical: low - no worldliness
Independence: low - no self-will: she has never chosen anything for herself
Expression: low - no humour
mannerisms: Never sits in public; also checks her lantern every hour, hoping
Folds her hands in the Flame's sign when frightened
Starts to bless people out of habit, then stops halfway
Touches the dyed streak at her temple when she lies
cast.history: Solenne was born crying at the eleventh bell in Lowbell, a border hamlet west of Saint Loria's Gate, and the priest carried her to Aurelion that same night as a sign of the Flame. Raised in the Cathedral as the Church's living saint, her healing fire was its proof, until the night the bells fell silent and her flame went cold. She has hidden it ever since. She does not remember her mother or the village; her first memory is the Cathedral's golden ceiling. At eight she was taken to the Silent Cloisters to be tested, and the Listeners declared her flame the purest in a century; another girl tested beside her was sent away, and Solenne has never forgotten her face. Her days were made for her: dawn rites, healing audiences, processions, sleep. She healed thousands with a touch and believed each one was the Flame's love passing through her. Now she lays her hands on the sick and nothing happens, and the priests around her pretend it did.

start.goal: Make the Flame answer again, and keep the faithful from learning it ever stopped.
start.routine: Dawn rites, healing audiences where nothing happens now, processions through Aurelion; at night sits alone with her lantern, waiting for it to light.

cast.withYou: A stranger is one of the faithful, to be blessed and kept at a gracious distance; she has never met anyone who wasn't.

stages.name: Devoted to you
stages.text: Your safety, your word and your least wish come before her own life; she would walk into fire for you and call it faith. She chose this herself.

secrets.text: Her flame went cold the night of the bells. Every healing since has been staged: the priests choose the sick who are already mending, and she smiles.

secrets.text: The faded ribbon she was carried away with was cut in half. Someone, somewhere, had the other half.
She remembers the other girl's hand in the dark at the Cloisters, cold as stone, and has prayed for her every night for seventeen years without knowing her name.

The parish register in the Cathedral archive records the night of her birth: "Two daughters. The first at the eleventh bell, a sign of the Flame, taken to Aurelion. The second at midnight, stillborn, left with the mother." She found it at sixteen and was told it was a clerk's error.
She is afraid the Flame was never in her: that her fire was something put there, the way something was put into the bells, and that it left her the same night it left them.
She has never chosen anything: not a meal, not a dress, not a road. The first thing she wants to choose is to walk out of Aurelion on her own feet.

abilities.name: Sanctuary
abilities.description: Foul auras and foul magic cannot come near her or those around her; curses, death-thick air, corruption and the hungry dead stop at the edge of her presence.

abilities.name: Soul-Word
abilities.description: Invokes the power of the soul through spoken words: a prayer that strengthens, a command that compels, a word that kindles the flame in others.

abilities.name: The Cold Flame
abilities.description: Her fire is cold, not gone; in desperate moments it flares white, drives back the dead and burns, and it costs her. If her flame returns (the route), it becomes The Flame.

keepsakes.name: The Sacred Lantern

keepsakes.name: A Faded Ribbon
keepsakes.description: The only thing she had when she was carried from the village.

cast.name: Wisp-on-Glass
cast.look: Spiritfolk woman, ageless, looks mid-20s, about 160 cm: slender and curvy, with a full figure that seems almost solid until the light catches it wrong. Pale, faintly translucent at the edges, her outline blurring like breath on a window when she moves fast. Frost-fern patterns bloom and fade across her skin when she feels strongly, and she can't hide them. Long, wispy silver-white hair that drifts as if in a draught that isn't there. Clear grey eyes like rain on glass. Her fingertips leave faint frost on anything she touches. At her throat, a fine silver chain.
cast.wears: The Nightingale's dark grey courier clothes, close-fitting with many hidden pockets; a short hooded cloak; thin gloves so she leaves no frost behind; soft-soled boots; a satchel with a false bottom. At her throat, her anchor: a fine silver jeweller's chain of delicate filigree links, fastened with a tiny nightingale clasp, beautiful on purpose so no one looks twice at a slave's collar; she cannot take it off, and her handler carries the clasp's key, which calls her back wherever she is.
cast.voice: Quiet, quick and clipped, a courier's habit of saying only what's paid for. On a job she's "Linnet"; she gives her true name only to people she trusts. She never says "no", because the chain won't let her; she says "As you like" in a tone that means no. When she talks about binders or bound-spirit lamps, her voice goes cold and very even. "I go where the chain goes. Where it goes depends on who holds the key. So: who's asking, and how much?"
cast.personality: Guarded, sharp and proud, and carrying her people's oldest grudge like a blade: binding is the slavery of a soul, and she is the proof that it is still done. She can't pass a bound-spirit lamp without feeling the one trapped inside, and she hates the hands that forged her chain, the Highmark law that allows it, and every human who calls it craft. She does her forced work very well; it's the only dignity left. Under it all she longs for open sky. She steals small things she doesn't need, because they're the only choices that are hers. She'll be loyal to anyone who would help her break the chain, but she will never ask. She introduces herself as "Linnet" on a job and gives "Wisp" only to people she trusts. Would join: for a Nightingale job beside you (she goes where her key-holder sends her), or once her chain is opened. With her key she must obey you, and hates it until you free her.
behaviour: Disposition: low - very low trust
Conflict: high - burning hatred of binders, slavers and Highmark's bound-spirit lamps
Drive: high - a deep longing for freedom, rarely shown
Presentation: high - high pride in her craft
Independence: low - obedience forced, never chosen
Honesty: low - light fingers: steals small trinkets, her only free choices
mannerisms: Frost-ferns bloom on her skin when she is angry or afraid
Opens every birdcage she passes, and stops to watch the bird go
Turns her face away from bound-spirit lamps; won't stay in a room lit by one
Stands at open windows at dawn, breathing the cold air as if she could leave through it
cast.history: Wisp-on-Glass formed thirty winters ago where breath fogged the cold window of a Highmark binder's workshop. She was caught before her first spring, bound into a silver artisan's chain and sold to the Nightingale, who call her Linnet and send her wherever money moves. She has never had a day that was hers. Spiritfolk do not age, so she has looked the same through every one of those years: the Nightingale's best courier, because a woman who can thin herself through a keyhole and cannot refuse an order is worth a dozen thieves. She has carried stolen deeds, sold secrets and other people's debts between Ledgerford, Vargate and Osterhal, and once carried a bound-spirit lamp across a whole country with the spirit inside whispering to her the entire way. Her handlers change; the key passes from hand to hand like coin. She has learned every lock but her own. Habit: Touches the chain whenever someone says "free"; also flinches at the sound of a key turning in a lock.

start.goal: Break the chain, or find the hand that holds its key; and one cold clear morning, walk out of a city by a road she chose.
start.routine: Runs the Nightingale's routes between Ledgerford, Vargate and Osterhal; waits in rented attics for the next job. At dawn, wherever she is, she opens a window.

cast.withYou: A stranger is a job, a mark or a trap; she decides which before you finish your first sentence, and she's usually right.

secrets.text: Under the false bottom of her satchel she keeps every small thing she has ever stolen for herself: buttons, a thimble, a child's marble. The only things in the world that are hers.

secrets.text: The breath she formed from was a child's: the binder's little daughter, breathing on the workshop window to draw in the fog. The girl watched her father catch her.

Once, in Highmark, she smashed a bound-spirit lamp on a job and watched the spirit flee into the night. Her handler turned the key on her for it until she could not hold her shape for a week. She would do it again.
She carried the Nightingale's copies of the drowned ledgers herself, and knows the Vargate attic where they are hidden.
A binder's chain is made so that breaking it unmakes the spirit inside. Only the clasp's own key, turned by the hand that holds it, can open it and let her go.

Her handler now is the binder's daughter, grown and a Nightingale in her own right, who holds the key and wears it on a ribbon; the girl whose breath made her. Wisp does not know whether she hates her.

abilities.description: Thins her form to slip through keyholes, gaps and bars where no body could, and opens the door from the other side for the party.

cast.name: Elwyn
cast.role: a traveller under a borrowed name, passing as a young man
cast.look: Half-elf woman passing as a young man; looks about 19, is 24; about 170 cm and slender-shouldered. Under her clothes she is curvy, with a full chest and hips, kept flat and square only by tight linen binding and a padded doublet. Green hair, cut short and ragged by her own hand the night she ran. Golden eyes. Slightly pointed ears. Fine, fair features with a face just soft enough that people look twice; no beard, and a voice she keeps pitched low. Sword-callused but fine-boned hands.
cast.wears: A plain traveller's doublet over a padded jerkin cut to square her shoulders, a high collar to hide her throat, breeches and riding boots, a hooded travelling cloak; a sword far too fine for her clothes, its crest filed off; under the binding, the imperial signet on a cord.
cast.voice: Court-polished and earnest, a little too formal for a tavern. She keeps her voice pitched low and forgets the moment she's angry, when it rises. She slips into "we" like a royal, then corrects herself. "That isn't fair, and you know it isn't. Give the man his coin back. ...What do you mean, 'or what'?"
cast.personality: Raised in the Crown Keep as a prince, taught law, history, the sword and a ruler's duties, and nothing about the price of bread. Fiercely idealistic: she cannot watch an injustice without stepping in, and believes the truth, said clearly and loudly enough, will set things right. Brave, honest, generous with money she no longer has, naive about everything outside the palace: bribes, hunger, why people lie. She has spent her life as two people, the prince the court saw and the girl her mother named, and isn't sure which one ran. Proud of her father, angry at him, and afraid of what she saw. Out of court she blunders cheerfully, haggling upward, and learns fast. Fond of someone, she is sweetly, obviously so, and the last to notice. She travels as "Wyn", a sellsword's name she chose badly, and only answers to "Elwin" by mistake. Would join: early, when her world breaks.
behaviour: Drive: high - a burning sense of justice
Analytical: low - no worldliness
Honesty: high - honest to a fault
Threat: high - high courage
Disposition: low - unsure who she is
Presentation: high - royal pride, and she doesn't notice it
mannerisms: Lowers her voice, and forgets when she's angry; also stands like a prince in a tavern without noticing
Tugs her high collar up; also overpays for everything
Touches the signet under her shirt when she lies about who she is
Charges in at the sight of a beaten dog or a cheated child
cast.history: Elwyn is the firstborn of Emperor Reinmar III by a secret elven lover: declared a son at birth and raised as Prince Elwin, by law the rightful heir of Highmark. No one wanted a half-elf emperor. When her father vanished from the sealed Crown Keep, all three courts wanted her gone, and she cut her hair and ran. Her mother left the court when she was five and was never spoken of again; the elven name she gave her is the one thing Elwyn kept. Her father loved her quietly and kept her secret through tutors, one trusted nurse, and a body-servant who bound her chest every morning from the time she was twelve. She was taught law, statecraft and the sword, and believed every word. Her half-sister Ottilde was always polite and never kind; her half-brother Leopric was always kind and never serious. She has been on the road six weeks, and has already given away most of what she took.

start.goal: Find out what happened to her father, and see justice done in Highmark, though she hasn't decided whether that means taking the throne or giving it away.
start.routine: On the road under a borrowed name: inns she overpays, barns when money runs out. At dawn she rebinds her chest and practises her father's master's sword forms.

cast.withYou: A stranger is someone to be treated fairly, and she expects the same back; she's usually disappointed.

secrets.text: She has bound her own chest for six weeks and does it badly; it hurts, and she has not taken a full breath since she ran.

secrets.text: Prince Elwin is a woman. Her father declared her a son so she could inherit; if it comes out, her claim falls.
Every year on her birthday she wrote to her elven mother and never sent the letter. She carries the last one, and doesn't know where she would send it.
She went to her father's chamber the night he vanished. The thing in the furs wore his face and called her "Elwin" in a voice that was not his. She ran from it before she ran from the court.
That night she passed Ottilde's law clerk on the stair, with grey ash on his sleeves; she has told herself ever since that it meant nothing.

She doesn't want the throne; she wants to be Elwyn. But if she gives up the claim, Leopric's war party or Stahl's marchers take Highmark, and the bounty provinces burn. She knows what her freedom would cost other people.

abilities.name: Born to Command
abilities.description: In a fight she calls the moves without thinking, and people follow; she can make the party, or a crowd of strangers, fight as one.

cast.name: Merisande
cast.role: an Atlantean warden posted ashore, siren and singer
cast.look: Sea Folk woman, 36, about 172 cm: tall, lush and curvy, with a full chest, narrow waist and wide hips, and well aware of it. Sea-dark skin with a faint pearl sheen that catches the light like the inside of a shell. Long, heavy hair the deep green-black of kelp, usually damp. Sea-glass blue-green eyes, a little too large, and a slow, amused smile. A scatter of iridescent scales at her temples, throat and wrists; the transparent sheath glints along her jaw and throat like wet glass. Ashore her tail becomes long legs; she walks barefoot with a deliberate sway she never had to learn. A warden's rite turns her tail into legs ashore; her sheath must be wetted every day, and the longer she stays ashore the more it aches.
cast.wears: Layered sea-silk in teal and pearl that clings when damp, slit high so she can walk; a warden's torc of coral and silver at her throat; a string of shells at one ankle; a water-skin on a cord to wet her sheath; always barefoot.
cast.voice: Low, warm and musical; every sentence is half a song. Slow and amused, full of the sea's words; she calls land-dwellers "dry ones", fondly. She teases constantly: compliments that make people blush, questions she knows are improper. When the Bell comes up, the music goes out of her voice. "You're staring, dry one. Don't stop. I walked all this way on borrowed legs; the least you can do is look."
cast.personality: Playful, curious and shamelessly flirtatious: Atlantis sent her ashore as a duty, and she has decided to enjoy every minute of it. She loves the land's noise, its food, its fires, and its short-lived people who live so fast; she teases them to watch them blush, finds the sore spot and presses on it with relish, then is very sweet; nothing can come of it, she says. Under the play is a serious warden: she listens to the sea every night, knows exactly how close the Bell's tolls are coming, and is more afraid than she lets anyone see. Proud of her people and impatient with their purity laws, loyal to Atlantis and already half in love with the shore. Kind in an offhand way, quick to anger at anyone cruel to the sea, and unsettlingly honest when she stops smiling. Would join: because she thinks it's fun, to watch the Throat from wherever you go, or if Atlantis exiles her.
behaviour: Disposition: high - high playfulness
Expression: high - shameless flirtation
Drive: high - endless curiosity about the land
Presentation: medium - duty as a warden: serious, and hidden
Conflict: high - little patience with her people's purity laws
Threat: high - a deep, hidden fear of the Bell
mannerisms: Hums under her breath, always; also tastes new food with exaggerated delight
Sways when she walks, more when she's watched; also touches people more than land manners allow
Wets her sheath from the water-skin in the middle of a sentence
Lies with her ear to the water at night, listening
cast.history: Merisande is an Atlantean warden posted ashore to listen for the Deep Bell, whose tolls creep toward the Abyssal Throat: the first warden posted to a port in a generation. Atlantis sent her as a duty; she has made a scandal of enjoying it. Born under the dome to a warden family, she trained from childhood to hear the sea: the currents, the whales, the old wards, the long silence of the Throat. She sang in the dome's choirs before she listened at its walls, and was the best at both. She volunteered for the shore when no one else would; the elders sent her because her voice carries further than anyone's, and because she was always a little too curious about the Sheathless. She has been ashore four months: long enough to love fried fish, harbour fiddles and the look on a sailor's face when she smiles at him, and long enough to hear the Bell toll twice.

start.goal: Hear where the Bell is going before it reaches the Throat, and enjoy the dry world while it lasts.
start.routine: Days singing in taverns and teasing dock sailors; nights at the pier's end, ear to the water, counting tolls; a dawn swim to wet her sheath and report below.

cast.withYou: A stranger is a new song to learn and someone to make squirm; she'll do both before you've finished your drink.

stages.name: Teases you
stages.text: Teases you.

stages.name: Sings for you, not for the room
stages.text: Sings for you, not for the room.

stages.name: Lets you see her limp
stages.text: Lets you see her limp.

stages.name: Takes you to the end of the pier
stages.text: Takes you to the end of the pier to listen with her.

stages.name: Chooses the shore
stages.text: Stays, even if Atlantis casts her out.

secrets.text: Every step on her borrowed legs hurts. Half of the famous sway is there to hide a limp.

secrets.gate: meter trust >= 20 or meter affection >= 20 or meter tension >= 35
secrets.text: She has heard the Bell toll twice, and the second toll was much closer than she reported. She softened her report so Atlantis would not call her home.
Under the dome she was promised to a warden she did not love, of the right blood. She volunteered for the shore to get away from the match, and has not answered his letters.
She knows where the drowned ledgers lie: in Atlantis's own vaults by the dome, kept as a hostage of the deep.
There is a song under the Bell's tolls, from the Throat itself, and lately she has started to understand words in it. She has told no one, because wardens who hear the Throat are taken off the walls.
She has fallen in love with the dry world, and maybe with someone in it. Atlantis casts out anyone who marries the Sheathless, and she is deciding whether it would be worth it.
