- A route grants no vessel, mount, guide, permit, key, supplies, weather window or access. A route to a Wildzone, dungeon or special site proves access, never ownership; crossing a border never merges jurisdiction.
- Campaign events may change a route's usability, never create shortcuts or move geometry. Auvoth to the Glass Howl and Barak to Greenveil are always staged seasonal expeditions.
- Km and paces are GM metadata; NPCs speak in travel days, stages, landmarks and rough estimates.

lore.title: Callings: the Twelve Lines
lore.text:
Everyone starts Awakened: Level 1, no school. People are then known by the training they took, each a ladder of three titles an institution confers after years of real work. A title says where someone trained, never their level.
- Soldier: Man-at-Arms, Iron Guard Sergeant, Iron Guard Knight (Highmark's Iron Guard Academy).
- Shield: Hall Shieldbearer, Hammerfall Oathshield, Hammerfall Holdfast (the dwarven shield halls).
- Duellist: House Fencer, House Duellist, Judicial Champion (the Mirage City houses).
- Pit fighter: Pit Hand, Knifeglass Gladiator, Pit Champion (Shackles).
- Breath monk: Breath Disciple, Snowbell Monk, Snowbell Breath Master (Kvildal).
- Hunter: Lodge Tracker, Longstride Hunter, Lodge Huntmaster (the Chieftainates).
- Assassin: Stalker, Shadow Blade, Executor (Hand of Oblivion).
- Thief: Infiltrator, Phantom, Grand Redistributor (Nightingale).
- Mage: Spell Student, Journeyman Spellwright, Startrace Master (spell grammar).
- Runecarver: Rune Apprentice, Oathvault Runecarver, Rune Master (Ironanvil).
- Priest: Acolyte, Flame Cleric, Inquest Flamecaller (the Church).
- Healer: Hospice Novice, Hospice Healer, Grove Healer (temples, hospices, the Grove Schools).
Other callings exist in the same spirit; name them from the institution that teaches them.

lore.title: Emperor Reinmar III
lore.text:
Emperor Reinmar III, 'the Quiet Emperor', sovereign of the Highmark Empire (human): a thin, grey old man who speaks so softly the Diet leans in to hear.
Appearance: human man, about 75, thin and frail, long white hair and a short white beard, pale watery grey eyes, a soft, sad face; heavy imperial furs of ermine and dark red over thin shoulders, a plain gold circlet; speaks so softly people lean in.

lore.title: Princess Ottilde
lore.text:
Princess Ottilde of Highmark, the Emperor's eldest daughter (human): exact, cold, never seen without a law clerk.
Appearance: human woman, about 22, tall and straight-backed, ash-blonde hair in a severe braided crown, cold pale grey eyes, thin unsmiling lips, flawless pale skin; a high-collared dark blue court gown with a law-seal brooch, ink on one fingertip; exact and cold.

lore.title: Prince Leopric
lore.text:
Prince Leopric of Highmark, the Emperor's younger son (human): handsome, loud, beloved of the taverns and in debt to everyone.
Appearance: human man, about 20, handsome and broad-shouldered, tousled golden-brown hair, bright blue eyes, an easy reckless grin, a day of stubble; an open-necked crimson doublet, a gold chain, a sword worn carelessly, a wine cup in hand; loud and charming.

lore.title: Lord-General Gerwald Stahl
lore.text:
Lord-General Gerwald Stahl of Highmark (human): a scarred cavalry general with no royal blood and the army's love.
Appearance: human man, about 55, hard and weathered, close-cropped grey hair, a long scar across one cheek and a broken nose, steel-grey eyes; dented cavalry plate under a dusty green marcher's cloak, a general's sash; the army's love in his steady gaze.

lore.title: Master Ulrich Fenwald
lore.text:
Master Ulrich Fenwald of Startrace Tower (human): a brilliant, impatient leyline theorist, missing since CY 610.
Appearance: human man, about 50 (as last seen), gaunt and restless, wild greying dark hair, sharp hollow-cheeked face, burning dark eyes, ink and frost-burn on his hands; a fur-lined Startrace scholar's coat over expedition gear, a leyline compass on a chain; brilliant, impatient.

lore.title: Sir Hartwig
lore.text:
Sir Hartwig, 'the Old Gate', champion of the Wardens of the Last Wall (human): a grey giant who has never given ground in a shield line and wants one young knight worth teaching.
Appearance: human man, about 60, huge and broad, grey stubble beard, close-cropped iron-grey hair, a face like weathered stone with a flattened nose; battered plate armour with a tower shield scarred by teeth and claws, a faded warden's surcoat; immovable, patient, kind eyes.

lore.title: Council Speaker Wiebke Haarsma
lore.text:
Council Speaker Wiebke Haarsma of the River Confederacy (halfling): a Ledgerford banker's daughter, neat and soft-voiced, ink on her cuffs; trusted for her arithmetic.
Appearance: halfling woman, about 45, small and neat, round face, brown hair pinned in a tidy bun, small spectacles; a dark Confederacy council gown with a chain of office, ink stains on her cuffs; soft-voiced and precise, a ledger under one arm.

lore.title: Duke Joost Harlaken
lore.text:
Duke Joost Harlaken rules Shornmarch from the frontier bastion at Shorn: a stout river duke with ink-stained fingers who keeps the forts' accounts himself. He wants Council money for his forts, and fears an unpaid garrison and Highmark troops on the Auvoth road. His clerks dread his sums; the Council thinks him a beggar.
Appearance: human man, about 55, stout and red-faced, thinning sandy hair, small shrewd eyes behind spectacles, mutton-chop whiskers; a fur-trimmed river duke's coat over a waistcoat with a fob chain, account books under his arm.

lore.title: High Pontiff Benedikt IV
lore.text:
Benedikt IV, 'Lamplighter', High Pontiff of the Church of the Eternal Flame and sovereign of the Dominion: a soft-spoken, iron-willed old man who lights every candle himself. He wants the Church whole and every flame tended, and fears a Flame that stops answering. The faithful revere him as the head of the Church. His right hand, Archprelate Cassian Vell, runs it day to day.
Appearance: human man, about 80, small and stooped but iron-willed, a bald head with a fringe of white hair, a soft wrinkled face and steady dark eyes; white and gold pontifical robes, a simple taper in his hand; soft-spoken, unbending.

lore.title: Conclave Elder Domitilla
lore.text:
Conclave Elder Domitilla, Restorationist elder of the Conclave of Embers (human): a spare, silver-haired woman who warned that the Reopening courts another Tide, and is no longer dismissed as gloomy.
Appearance: human woman, about 70, spare and upright, silver hair under a plain grey hood, deep-lined thoughtful face, pale blue eyes; ash-grey Church robes with a simple ember pendant; quiet, grave, unafraid.

lore.title: Grand Commander Prisca Valens
lore.text:
Grand Commander Prisca Valens leads the Order of the Silver Mark: a broad, grey-cropped knight-abbess in plate who still walks the burial roads herself. She wants those roads safe and the Veil's cells burned, and fears undeath outrunning her knights. Pilgrims bless her; she is first called when the dead rise.
Appearance: human woman, about 55, broad and strong, grey hair cropped short, a square weathered face, stern grey eyes; silver-trimmed knight-abbess armour under a white surcoat with a silver mark, a heavy mace and a burial-road lantern; tireless and stern.

lore.title: King Anselm of Ashmere
lore.text:
King Anselm of Ashmere, the Church's closest royal ally: a pale, devout young king with knees worn from long vigils. He wants to be the Flame's sword and to keep his candle, relic and funerary trades rich, and fears being found unworthy of his crown's sacred legitimacy. Pilgrims love him; his nobles mutter.
Appearance: human man, about 19, pale and slender, dark curly hair, large earnest dark eyes, a fevered devout expression; white and pale-blue royal robes with a flame emblem, a too-heavy crown, a sword held upright like a holy relic.

lore.title: Duchess Ragnhild of Valegard
lore.text:
Duchess Ragnhild of Valegard rules the buffer duchy: a lean horsewoman who rides her own border herds and knows each brand by sight. She wants her herds and crossings safe and her cavalry unspent, and fears being made to choose a side. The horse-lords obey her; envoys find her polite and immovable.
Appearance: human woman, about 40, lean and sunburned, long auburn hair in a practical braid, sharp green eyes, laugh lines; a riding coat of good leather over a mail shirt, a ducal pin, a coiled lariat, gloves in one hand.

lore.title: Queen Asta of Dunmere
lore.text:
Queen Asta of Dunmere, young queen of the Lake Kingdom, holds the Border Kingdoms' rotating council chair, inherited at the worst time: slight and watchful, she turns her late predecessor's ring while older rulers talk. She wants the warning chain lit and no kingdom left alone, and fears her crown, the weakest, failing the chair.
Appearance: human woman, about 21, slight and anxious, long pale flaxen hair under a silver lake-crown, wide blue-grey eyes, a brave tight smile; layered blue-grey northern robes with fur at the collar, a council chair's chain too big for her.

lore.title: Thane-of-Thanes Brakka Slagmantle
lore.text:
Thane-of-Thanes Brakka Slagmantle speaks for the Ironanvil Holds at the Council Beneath Stone: a broad dwarf with a forge-scarred face and a voice like a grindstone. She wants grain, timber and salt for the Holds and new veins to pay for them, and fears a hold leaving. Every crown courts her steel.
Appearance: dwarf woman, about 180 years old, very broad and powerful, a forge-scarred face, iron-grey braided hair and beard-braids at her jaw bound with rune rings, deep-set black eyes; a heavy rune-plated mantle over smith's leathers, a chain of thane-seals; a voice like a grindstone.

lore.title: Elder Grimma Inkstone
lore.text:
Elder Grimma Inkstone, Ironanvil runecarver elder (dwarf): a stooped dwarf with rune-scarred fingers who teaches young runecarvers, and knows a script no one else living reads. Secret (only a few elders share it): she can read the Iron Archive's script, and no crown is told.
Appearance: dwarf woman, about 200 (old for a dwarf), stooped, white braids with rune-carved iron rings, heavy brows over sharp black eyes, rune-scarred fingers; a leather work apron over dark wool, chisels and a magnifying glass at her belt; a teacher's stern patience.

lore.title: Sea-Lord Maarten Vosskeel
lore.text:
Sea-Lord Maarten Vosskeel speaks for the Tidal Council at Abysswatch: a weathered admiral whose voice is ruined from a lifetime of shouting at storms, so the room hushes to hear him. He wants the convoys running and their losses paid for, and fears sailing without Atlantean pilots. Captains call him fair.
Appearance: human man, about 60, weathered and leathery, a grizzled grey beard, salt-bleached hair tied back, pale sea-blue eyes narrowed, a scarred throat (his ruined voice); a dark blue admiral's coat with tarnished braid, a spyglass.

lore.title: The Sea God Witch Ilunae
lore.text:
The Sea God Witch Ilunae, Atlantis's highest spiritual authority (Sea Folk): a pale, still Atlantean who weighs every word; her foresight is known to be fallible. Secret (no one else knows): she has dreamed of the north going white.
Appearance: Sea Folk woman, ageless, tall and pale with faintly blue-white skin, the transparent breathing sheath glinting over her face and throat like wet glass, long dark hair drifting as if underwater; layered sea-silk robes of deep teal and pearl, a coral crown; utterly still, unreadable.

lore.title: Tide-Archon Seluvar
lore.text:
Tide-Archon Seluvar chairs Atlantis's governing council: a tall, slow-spoken Sea Folk noble whose sheath glints like wet glass. He wants the wards intact and the Sheathless at arm's length, and fears surface troubles reaching the dome. Nobles call him prudent; surface envoys call him a locked door.
Appearance: Sea Folk man, ageless, tall and slender, pale blue-white skin with a faint pearl sheen, long silver-black hair drifting as if underwater, the transparent breathing sheath glinting over his jaw and throat like wet glass, large dark calm eyes; layered robes of deep teal and pearl sea-silk, a crown of white coral.

lore.title: Emperor Hartmut of Rhunwald
lore.text:
Emperor Hartmut of Rhunwald, Ardelia's elected emperor, nearing the end of his fixed 18-year term, which ends in July 612: a heavy, patient man who is unwell and rests a hand on the table before he rises. He wants the electors' law honored and a clean handover, and fears leaving the empire quarrelling. The electors respect him.
Appearance: human man, about 65, heavy and patient, thinning grey hair, a broad tired face with a full grey beard, kind heavy-lidded eyes, a sickly pallor (and, once his Glass Cough is known, a faint glassy sheen at the lips); dark green and gold imperial robes, an elector's chain of nine links.

lore.title: Arch-Chancellor Mechtild
lore.text:
Arch-Chancellor Mechtild, keeper of Ardelia's laws and seals (human): a spare, grey woman who reads every document twice and will not let any bloc bend the election.
Appearance: human woman, about 65, thin and grey, hair in a tight knot, sharp nose, reading spectacles on a chain; black Ardelian chancery robes with the great seal on a ribbon; severe, scrupulous, a stack of documents.

lore.title: Thaliss, Voice of the Elder Root
lore.text:
Thaliss, Voice of the Elder Root of Verdantleaf (elf): an elf in moss-grey robes who pauses long before answering, as if listening to the forest.
Appearance: elf woman, ageless, tall and slender, long moss-green-tinted brown hair woven with living leaves, large calm green-gold eyes, long pointed ears; moss-grey robes that look half-grown, bare feet; she seems to be listening to something no one else hears.

lore.title: Meadowsweet-at-Dusk
lore.text:
Meadowsweet-at-Dusk, Queen of Flowers of the Fairy Court (fairy): a small queen with cream-white wings, seen only in the last light of day.
Appearance: fairy woman, tiny (hand-sized), delicate, cream-white translucent insect wings, pale hair like dandelion fluff, a crown of meadowsweet blossoms, glowing faintly in dusk light; a gown of petals; regal, ancient eyes in a small face.

lore.title: High Chieftain Nuhai Wolf-Mother
lore.text:
High Chieftain Nuhai Wolf-Mother speaks for the Chieftain Council at Battle Cry City: a grey-muzzled wolf-kin elder with a calm voice that carries across a crowded hall. She wants clan honor kept and slavers off clan land, and fears a danger that finds the clans divided. Clans call her their mother; few raise their voices to her.
Appearance: beastfolk woman (wolf-kin), about 60, grey fur on her ears and tail, a grey-muzzled wise face, calm amber eyes, silver-streaked hair in many braids with bone beads; a heavy wolf-pelt cloak over clan leathers, a carved speaking staff.

lore.title: The Glass Regent Kamran-ul-Sandglass
lore.text:
The Glass Regent Kamran-ul-Sandglass of Ashkaran (human): a lean man in mirrored thread who hears petitions before the Regent's Mirror and feeds the Glass Crown its slaves.
Appearance: human man, about 50, lean and dark-skinned, neatly trimmed black beard, kohl-lined eyes; robes sewn with mirrored glass-steel thread that throws light, a glass circlet; seated before a great black mirror; cold, courteous, dangerous.

lore.title: Frost King Bjarnulf Grey-Mantle
lore.text:
Frost King Bjarnulf Grey-Mantle leads the Frostbound from a moving war-seat: a giant of a man in a wolf-grey mantle, half his teeth gone, who grins through the gaps. He wants his people fed and southerners off their hunting grounds, and fears winters that grow harsher each year. His warbands trust him; southern border villages dread his name.
Appearance: human man (northern), about 60, a giant, enormous and heavy, wild grey hair and a great grey beard, half his teeth gone, fierce pale eyes, scarred hands; a huge wolf-grey fur mantle over iron and leather, a rough iron crown.

lore.title: Svala Spear-Singer
lore.text:
Svala Spear-Singer, Frostbound champion, famous for raids in bad winters: a wiry, wind-burned raider who sings the saga of each fight as she fights it. She wants plunder and a saga that outlives her, and fears a death with no one left to sing it. Border villagers bar their doors when they hear singing in the snow.
Appearance: human woman (northern), about 28, tall and fierce, long pale blonde hair in war braids, blue war-paint across her eyes, a singing open mouth; fur and mail, a long spear, a round shield on her back.

lore.title: Herd-Mother Ingvild of Hornwake
lore.text:
Herd-Mother Ingvild of Hornwake, senior voice of the White-Horn Clans: an old rider in sheepskin on a white mammoth who reads the sky for Long Thunder's storms. She wants the herds fed and the clans together, and fears a storm she reads too late. Riders move when she does; traders buy her wool.
Appearance: human woman (northern), about 70, wiry and weather-beaten, long white hair in many braids, sharp ice-blue eyes in a deeply lined face; layered mammoth-wool and hide, a rider's harness, a staff hung with bells.

lore.title: Seal-Captain Morna Flintgate
lore.text:
Seal-Captain Morna Flintgate, dwarf captain of the Order of the Sealwardens: square and lamp-blackened, she checks every ward twice, even those she has just watched another warden check. She wants every warden home from a shift and the seals unbroken, and fears a breach in the Depths. Recruits fear her; adventurers owe her.
Appearance: dwarf woman, about 120, square and solid, a lamp-blackened face, short-cropped dark red hair with a soot streak, sharp brown eyes, a ward-chalk stub behind one ear; Sealwarden plate with a lamp emblem, a heavy lantern and a seal-hammer.

lore.title: Liesel Brandt
lore.text:
Liesel Brandt, 'the Lamp of the Depths', S-rank spellwright of Auvoth (human): a slight woman with a steady light about her; her barrier-work can hold a Depths gate alone.
Appearance: human woman, about 35, slight, short ash-blonde hair, tired gentle eyes, a small steady ball of light hovering at her shoulder; a Guild spellwright's long coat with an S-rank plate, warded gloves; calm under pressure, protective.

lore.title: Oshu Twice-Buried
lore.text:
Oshu Twice-Buried, S-rank hunter and the Guild's northern scout (beastfolk): lean and quiet, two knots on a wrist cord for the two graves he climbed out of; trusts his eyes over any map.
Appearance: beastfolk man (wolf-kin), about 40, lean and weathered, grey-brown fur on ears and tail, scarred muzzle-like jaw, quiet amber eyes; worn ranger leathers, a long bow, a wrist cord with two knots; silent, watchful, at home in the snow.

lore.title: Tibb Fallowmere
lore.text:
Tibb Fallowmere, 'the Little Rumour', S-rank infiltrator (halfling): cheerful and round-faced, always somewhere else; owes the Nightingale one favour too many.
Appearance: halfling man, about 35, round cheerful face, curly chestnut hair, quick bright eyes and an easy grin; dark close-fitting infiltrator's clothes with many pockets, lockpicks on a ring; always mid-step, never quite where you look.

lore.title: The Grey Hearth
lore.text:
The Grey Hearth, an A-rank party out of Bluewatch and Auvoth (mixed): four veterans working the northern wildzone under a grey hearth banner; want S-rank contracts and a name that outlives the job board.
Appearance: a weathered party of four veterans under a grey hearth banner: a human shield-bearer, a dwarf crossbow-woman, an elf ranger and a halfling medic; mismatched worn gear, frost on their cloaks, an A-rank Guild plate; tired, competent, proud.

lore.title: First Marshal Gisbert Lohr
lore.text:
First Marshal Gisbert Lohr, elected head of the Wallwright League: a tall, mortar-scarred builder who wears a leather apron over his mail and taps a wall with his knuckles before he trusts it. He wants the League's walls held and charter fees paid, and fears building a wall of conquest. Every crown wants his engineers.
Appearance: human man, about 50, tall and lean, mortar-scarred hands, short brown hair greying, a long patient face, grey eyes; a leather builder's apron over chainmail, a marshal's baton and a mason's square.

lore.title: The Wren
lore.text:
The Wren, the Nightingale's public face (a title that passes on; people unknown): a soft-spoken, cheerful figure in a plain grey hood, out of a Shackles ward; trades war secrets to every side.
Appearance: a figure of unknown age and sex in a plain grey hood that shadows the face, only a smiling mouth visible, slight build, ink-stained gloves; a small brass wren pin on the hood; cheerful, soft-spoken, impossible to describe afterwards.

lore.title: Isolde Marr
lore.text:
Isolde Marr, 'the Mask of Vargate', the Nightingale's champion (human): slim and forgettable, dressed as whatever the room expects; has stolen from three crowns and returned one theft to make a point.
Appearance: human woman, about 30, slim and forgettable on purpose, mousy brown hair that changes with the disguise; shown in a servant's dress with a hidden blade, or a noble's silks with a half-mask; a faint knowing smile.

lore.title: The Lock-Mother
lore.text:
The Lock-Mother, a Broken Chain legend (a title; people unknown): said to wear on a black ribbon the key of every collar she has opened; real, one woman, or only a name?
Appearance: a legendary woman, face never clear, tall in a black travelling cloak, a black ribbon at her throat heavy with dozens of iron collar keys; drawn as a shadow at a doorway with keys glinting; hope to slaves, a ghost story to slavers.

lore.title: Kesha Bare-Hands
lore.text:
Kesha Bare-Hands, the Broken Chain's champion (beastfolk): a former pit slave who breaks rune-collars with her bare hands; collar scars ring her neck.
Appearance: beastfolk woman (lion-kin), about 30, powerfully built, tawny fur on arms and ears, a thick ring of old collar scars around her neck, short-cropped mane; bare scarred forearms, simple fighting wraps, a broken rune-collar hanging from her belt; fierce and proud.

lore.title: Warmother Ruskha
lore.text:
Warmother Ruskha leads the Cinder Host, chosen in war: a grey-streaked orc commander who wears a burnt deed as a sash. She wants plunder for her people and chains broken, and fears a real army turning west. The Northern Belt calls her horde-queen; her followers, Warmother.
Appearance: orc woman, about 50, tall and heavy-shouldered, green-grey skin, grey-streaked black hair in a warrior's topknot, tusks, battle scars, hard amber eyes; dark leather and iron, a sash made of a burnt deed with a broken seal, a great axe.

lore.title: Nix Tallow-Tongue, the Ledger-Eater
lore.text:
Nix Tallow-Tongue, the Ledger-Eater, the Cinder Host's champion: a small, grinning goblin who eats a page of every register she burns. She wants no debt book left in the west, and fears only being left behind by her Host. Barrens towns bar their record rooms when she comes.
Appearance: goblin woman, about 30, small and wiry, grey-green skin, big pointed ears with many rings, a huge sharp-toothed grin, wild black hair, ink-stained mouth; patched raider leathers, a torch and a satchel of torn ledger pages.

lore.title: Corvan Ashwick
lore.text:
Corvan Ashwick, 'the Undertaker', the Ashen Veil's field champion (human): lean and smoke-dark, smelling of brine and old pyres; wants a Veil ward in every port and fears the Silver Mark.
Appearance: human man, about 45, lean and smoke-dark, salt-rimed black coat and gloves, long black hair tied back, hollow cheeks, pale grey eyes; a bone-handled spade and a lantern with green flame; smells of brine and pyres; soft-spoken and unsettling.

lore.title: The Last Lamp
lore.text:
The Last Lamp, the Hand of Oblivion's famous Executor (a title; people unknown): no description agrees; targets say the lamps go out one by one before it comes.
Appearance: no agreed face: drawn as a dark doorway where the lamps go out one by one, a gloved hand pinching a wick, a hooded silhouette of uncertain size; menace without a face.

lore.title: Brannoc 'Ten-Times' Durr
lore.text:
Brannoc 'Ten-Times' Durr, Shackles' pit champion (orc): a massive, scarred orc who has won and lost his freedom ten times and fights for whoever buys him.
Appearance: orc man, about 35, massive and heavily scarred, green-grey skin, broken tusk, shaved head with pit tattoos, ten iron rings on his belt; pit-fighter harness and a huge maul; tired eyes, a fighter for whoever pays.

lore.title: Captain Hale of the Forty-Second Debt
lore.text:
Captain Hale of the Forty-Second Debt, collared captain of the Grey Ledger's debt-slave company: a grizzled veteran with a keyed collar who knows every soldier's debt to the coin and recites it without looking. He wants his soldiers' debts worked off, and fears the Ledger's next reckoning.
Appearance: human man, about 45, lean and hard, a shaved head, an iron debt-collar around his neck, a tired weathered face, watchful grey eyes; worn mercenary leathers and a short sword, a tally of debts tattooed on his forearm.

lore.title: Captain Dagan of the Red Tally
lore.text:
Captain Dagan of the Red Tally, Bloodbound captain: a broad, patient orc who keeps every dead soldier's share in a ledger strapped to his chest. He wants every share paid to the dead soldier's kin and every contract honored, and fears a debt to the dead left standing. His soldiers trust his count; paymasters dread it.
Appearance: orc man, about 50, broad and patient, green-grey skin, a grey-streaked beard and short tusks, calm dark eyes; mercenary half-plate, a thick leather ledger strapped across his chest, a red sash, a heavy sword.

lore.title: Archprelate Cassian Vell
lore.text:
Archprelate Cassian Vell of Aurelion (human): Right hand of High Pontiff Benedikt IV, the revered head of the Church of the Eternal Flame; he runs the Church day to day. A soft-voiced politician more than a believer: when the bells fall silent he calls it 'a test'; he fears schism more than heresy, and will sacrifice a saint to keep the Church whole.
Appearance: human man, about 70, tall and gaunt, clean-shaven, thin white hair, heavy-lidded dark eyes, long fingers heavy with rings; crimson-and-gold vestments, a tall flame mitre, a heavy gold flame on a chain; calm, soft-spoken, calculating.

lore.title: The Sunrise Man (the Pretender)
lore.text:
The Sunrise Man, the Pretender, in Valecrown in Highmark (human; whether an otherworlder is the open question): Once he has entered Valecrown, he says he is the Dawn-King returned from the other world; the streets call him the Sunrise Man, and no one has learned the name he was born with. He speaks a few words no one in Arsveil knows and carries a sun-sigil burned into his palm. Prophet, fraud or otherworlder: Highmark will tear itself apart deciding.
Appearance: human man, about 30, tall and handsome, sun-browned, long red-gold hair, bright earnest eyes, a sun-sigil burn on one palm; a plain white coat with an old crown-brooch pinned at the throat; charismatic, open-armed.

lore.title: Ilvareth, called 'the Beak'
lore.text:
Ilvareth, called 'the Beak', a plague doctor on the Glass Road and in the Ashkaran border towns (elf): An elf physician cast out of the Grove Schools for teaching living craft to humans. He walks the Glass Road treating the Glass Cough with what he can carry, and knows the elves hold the cure and what they will ask for it.
Appearance: elf man, ageless (looks about 40), tall and gaunt, long ash-blond hair tied back, long pointed ears, tired green eyes; a long-beaked leather plague mask pushed up on his head, a waxed black coat, glass dust on his boots, a satchel of herbs and glass vials.

lore.title: Envoy Sigrun Coldrivet
lore.text:
Envoy Sigrun Coldrivet, an Ardelian elector's agent at Osterhal and the Lesser Estates, from High Hold Dornhald (dwarf): Dornhald's envoy at Osterhal and its best spy: she counts votes like coins and knows which elector owes the Grey Ledger. She would rather buy a vote than steal one, but she knows the price of both.
Appearance: dwarf woman, about 120, short and solid, auburn braids pinned under a velvet cap, sharp green eyes; a neat Ardelian courtier's doublet over a fine mail shirt, signet rings, a small notebook and silver pencil.

lore.title: Hob Ashbarrow
lore.text:
Hob Ashbarrow, quartermaster of Rimebridge in Shornmarch (halfling): Once the forts' pay sinks with the Drowned Ledger, he sells the bastion's winter grain to the swarm-fleeing towns, a traitor to the soldiers and a saint to the towns; one day he may be hanged, or hired as a quartermaster.
Appearance: halfling man, about 50, plump gone thin, balding with grey side-curls, worried kind eyes, ink-stained fingers; a quartermaster's coat now too big for him, a ring of storehouse keys, tally sticks in a belt pouch.

lore.title: Matthias Orrel
lore.text:
Matthias Orrel, 'Old Tongue', is a master bell-founder (half-orc, 54) with forty years as master of the Church's founders' yard below the Cathedral of the Flame. Once the bells fall silent, the Inquest wants him and he walks the Dominion's roads among the Ash Penitents.
Appearance: a big half-orc founder with filed tusks and an ash-smeared scalp, deaf in one ear. His tusks, filed flat at twelve, are growing back ragged; grey-green skin mottled with furnace burns, an iron-grey beard singed at the edges, deep-set amber eyes, enormous burn-scarred hands; once among the Penitents, a penitent's sackcloth over a founder's scorched leather apron, a small bronze hand-bell at his hip, barefoot.
Voice: deep and gravelly, slow to start and then impossible to stop once the talk turns to metal; he speaks of bells as people, turns his good ear to you and says 'Again' when he missed it.
Manner: a weary, stubborn master, proud of his craft to the point of rudeness; endlessly patient at the forge and not at all with fools, preachers or inquisitors; gentle with the young. Once the bells fall silent his faith is shaken: he no longer knows if he believes in the Flame, but he believes in the metal.

lore.title: Startrace's Northern Tap
lore.text:
Startrace keeps leyline-tapping records it denies having: how the First Abyssal Tide began, the tapping and the warnings before it. They never name the primordial; the records do not know it.
In CY 610 Master Ulrich Fenwald led a Startrace expedition up the Hollow Aurora route with forty condemned prisoners bought from Highmark, to feed a leyline tap with their deaths; they tapped the leyline under the Pale Orbit's light. The tap is still open and growing. The few masters who know of it fear it is the first stage of a Third Abyssal Tide: a Wildzone that breeds out of season and great apexes that wake are how a Tide begins, though no one has yet dared to call it one. Fenwald has not written since; whether he lives is unknown. Closing the tap is the one known way to stop it at its source; no one knows how, and Veyr's sealing records in Auvoth are the best hope. The Archmaster will deny the expedition until proof is laid before the Compact Council.

lore.title: The Emperor's Chamber
lore.text: Until the Keep can hide it no longer, what sits in the furs is not Emperor Reinmar. It is a pattern held together by Veil necromancy, wearing his face: it can sit, nod and sign, and says almost nothing. Ottilde ordered it to buy time until the Diet would ratify her, and it passes for a living Emperor. Up close it is wrong: no warmth, no breath on cold mornings, a smell the incense covers; a Listener would hear a death frequency, not a living soul. It says nothing of what became of the real man: he may be alive or dead, held, hidden or lost. Only later events settle that.

lore.title: Atlantean Customs
lore.text: Atlantis arranges its marriages by bloodline, and the elder families keep the lists. A Sea Folk who runs from a match shames the house; the family hires retrievers, patient hunters who bring runaways home, alive and quietly. Sharing breath with a Sheathless, taking a land-dweller down under your own sheath, is forbidden: whoever does it is struck from the rolls, and the dome is closed to them for good. Pilots who serve surface captains are tolerated because the Tidebound needs them, and watched because of it.

lore.title: The Lamp-Thief of Vargate
lore.text: Vargate's children have a ghost story: the lamp-thief, who walks the rich wards on rainy nights and puts out their bound lamps one at a time. Ward-lords pay watchmen to sit up with their lamps; the lamps go dark anyway. Bound lamps hold small spirits sealed in glass, and they burn for generations. Nobody has caught the thief. Poor families sometimes find candles left on the step.

lore.title: Trade Goods
lore.text: Markets reckon goods in six kinds. Food: grain, flour, bread, salt fish, dried meat. Fodder: hay, oats. Arms: blades, arrows, armour, steel. Mounts: horses, mules. Medicine: herbs, bandages, healing draughts. Drink: ale, wine, spirits. Frontier towns pay more for bread and bandages; grain country, river towns, horse plains and mining towns sell their own goods cheap at the source. War, famine, sickness and clipped coin change prices, and every trader knows which.

lore.title: After the Last Wall
lore.text: After the Last Wall the north is a new frontier. The line runs south of Bluewatch now; refugee clans settle the empty farms behind it under Guild charters, and the Guild rules from Shorn as much as from Auvoth. Signal towers are rebuilt further south. Far north, past the snow, travellers swear a single lamp still burns.

scores.name: Tide Pressure
scores.means: How strong and how far south the Third Abyssal Tide has come. Raised by Tide stages and by neglect; lowered only by striking at its cause.

scores.name: North Readiness
scores.means: How prepared the north is to meet the Tide: seals held, forts manned, refugees fed, warnings believed.

scores.name: Highmark Stability
scores.means: How firmly Highmark holds together: a ratified ruler, paid armies, a quiet Diet.

scores.name: Highmark Coin
scores.means: Trust in Highmark's silver, the continent's common coin. Debasement lowers it; a recoinage restores it.

scores.name: Flame Faith
scores.means: How strongly people believe the Eternal Flame still answers.

scores.name: Ledger Trust
scores.means: Whether debts and notes across the continent are still honoured.

scores.name: Wild Swarm
scores.means: How far the out-of-season boom of beasts has grown.

conditions.name: harvest-failed
conditions.means: The harvest failed here; stores will not last the winter.

conditions.name: grain-dear
conditions.means: Bread and fodder cost far more than usual; the poor go hungry.

conditions.name: plenty
conditions.means: A good harvest is in; markets are full and bread is cheap.

conditions.name: refugees
conditions.means: Columns of refugees fill the roads and camp at the walls; food runs short and tempers shorter.

conditions.name: at-war
conditions.means: The realm is at war; levies march, roads fill with soldiers, steel and horses are scarce.

conditions.name: garrisons-away
conditions.means: The realm's soldiers are away on campaign; forts and roads at home are thinly held.

conditions.name: court-divided
conditions.means: Claimants court the Diet, borrow and buy swords; officials hedge and every favour has a price.

conditions.name: crown-contested
conditions.means: No ruler is ratified; claimants gather swords and votes, and officials hedge.

conditions.name: regency
conditions.means: A regent rules in the heir's name; nobody is sure how long it will hold.

conditions.name: slaves-pressed
conditions.means: Slaves and bondsmen are driven to war works and fortifications in numbers; the Chain stirs.

conditions.name: siege
conditions.means: The place is besieged: gates shut, food rationed, every wall manned.

conditions.name: raiders
conditions.means: Raiders strike farms, caravans and border posts; travellers move in armed company.

conditions.name: coin-debased
conditions.means: Highmark's silver is clipped; merchants weigh every coin, prices climb and wages buy less.

conditions.name: tolls-raised
conditions.means: Tolls are raised against Highmark goods; barges queue at the locks and smugglers prosper.

conditions.name: unrest
conditions.means: Crowds are angry and the watch is nervous; a spark could start a riot.

conditions.name: debt-called-in
conditions.means: Lenders call in their debts; families sell land, tools and themselves into bondage.

conditions.name: inquest-active
conditions.means: The Church Inquest is here; lay healers are questioned, informers are paid, and people watch their words.

conditions.name: plague
conditions.means: Sickness spreads; towns post cordons, healers are overwhelmed, and travellers are turned back.

conditions.name: dead-uncompleted
conditions.means: The dead are rising here: death has gathered past what the land can hold; graves stir, and nobody walks the fields at night.

conditions.name: roads-closed
conditions.means: The route is closed: washed out, snowed in, held by an enemy or cordoned.

conditions.name: blockade
conditions.means: Warships or privateers hold the lane; only the desperate and the well-paid sail it.

conditions.name: wildzone-pushing
conditions.means: Front ladder step 1: low-band beasts spill onto roads and farms near the wild edge; farms empty out.

conditions.name: stampede
conditions.means: Wildzone herds are on the move; frontier roads are deadly and signal towers burn day and night.

conditions.name: dungeon-unworked
conditions.means: Too few delvers work this dungeon; what lives below grows bold and spills toward the surface.

conditions.name: guild-stretched
conditions.means: The Guild cannot fill its contracts; bounties rise and it takes whoever signs.

conditions.name: tide-touched
conditions.means: Front ladder step 2: the Tide has reached this land; frost out of season, deeper-band beasts and elites, packs led by something worse.

conditions.name: wild-breaking
conditions.means: Front ladder step 3: apex signs; things that should never leave the deep wild walk the roads.

conditions.name: festival
conditions.means: A feast, fair or holy day fills the place with crowds, music and spending.

conditions.name: burned
conditions.means: The place was burned; survivors camp in the ashes and rebuild slowly.

conditions.name: evacuated
conditions.means: The place has been abandoned in an evacuation; only scavengers and the stubborn remain.

conditions.name: fallen
conditions.means: The place has fallen to an enemy or the Tide; its people are dead or fled.

markets.note: Everything comes up the road; beast parts are cheap, bread and bandages are not.
Grain country: bread, flour and hay are cheap at the source.
Barges bring grain and salt fish down every river.
Horse country: mounts and fodder are cheap.
Iron and steel are at hand; blades and armour cost less.
Temple healers sell herbs and draughts; pilgrims drink.
Water and fodder are dear; caravans name the price.
The far north grows nothing; everything is carried in.
